548	## 4. Evaluation and proof verification
549	
550	The deterministic evaluator consumes only the Plan-bound, schema-admitted
551	finite fact views, Coverage, imported evidence, declarative program, policy and
552	waivers. The declarative rule program defines the exact subject enumeration,
553	relation/rung, typed field filter, quantifier, deterministic work bound and
554	emission condition for each predicate. Query planning is an optimization only:
555	a retained full-scan reference must agree on selected facts. Neither a provider
556	nor a witness supplies its own expected result or filter. All consumed data are
557	listed in the proof's evaluationInputRefs; no hidden lookup is allowed.
558	
559	A predicate proof binds rule, subject, predicate, operation, admitted inputs,
560	scopes, value and a retained witness digest. The closed witness record contains
561	schemaVersion=2, program predicate digest, sorted matching fact IDs, sorted
562	Coverage IDs, optional integer count limit and sorted child-predicate IDs.
563	The program predicate digest is the §3 `program-predicate` record, which addresses
564	the exact node of the admitted rule program this proof discharges; the predicate
565	ID and the child predicate IDs are that section's node addresses, not free
566	labels. An atomic witness names no children; boolean witnesses name only earlier
567	nodes in the same subject/rule DAG, and each named child must itself be proven
568	for the same rule and subject. Predicate IDs are unique and the DAG is bounded
569	by the rule program's admitted work bound. Witness facts must be exactly those
570	selected by the program over the complete admitted view, not merely a subset
571	chosen by the producer. Counts count distinct selected fact IDs. The verifier
572	recomputes scope membership, matches, completeness and each result, and then
573	recomputes finding fingerprints, findings, rule outcomes and aggregate verdict.
574	Missing witness bytes is retention loss, not a false predicate.
575	
576	| Predicate | Positive/complete case | Incomplete case |
577	|---|---|---|
578	| exists | true on a matching fact; false only on complete absence | true on a known match, otherwise indeterminate |
579	| none | false on a known match; true only on complete absence | false on a known match, otherwise indeterminate |
580	| count-at-most N | false once more than N distinct matches exist; true when complete count ≤ N | false above N, otherwise indeterminate |
581	| all-covered | true only with admitted resolution-complete coverage for the requested universe/rung | indeterminate |
582	| and / or / not | strong Kleene three-valued logic; false dominates and, true dominates or | unresolved value propagates unless dominated |
583	
584	Completeness means the native contract's examined partition **and** resolution
585	and closed-world requirements. An unresolved `m[k]()` can never establish
586	no-consumer merely because the enumerator visited all subjects. Runtime unhit
587	observations never supply universal static completeness. A rule expression that
588	is true produces its declared outcome; findings arise only from the program's
589	emission condition. A false condition is a retained no-match proof. An
590	indeterminate required predicate is retained with typed deficiency. A schema,
591	identity or interpreter fault is an operational failure, not a fourth logical
592	truth value and not an authoritative Run. Aggregate policy fail dominates
593	indeterminate, which dominates pass; a required operational fault has D9's
594	operational precedence even if other steps have committed failing Runs.
595	
596	Before sealing, the host independently replays the admitted deterministic
597	program against the retained closure and compares the complete normalized
598	result (all predicate outcomes, omissions, findings and verdict), not just a
599	checksum supplied by the producer. This verifier is first-party trusted code;
600	this is reproducible verification, not a proof of mathematical soundness or a
601	sandbox against a malicious host. Semantic conformance uses independent
602	oracles and mutation cases. The exact evaluator executable, declarative program,
603	input closure and witness bytes are retained, so an independent installation
604	can replay without trusting the original result flags. No old Python route
605	region is executed to decide product authority.
606	
607	Verification reads retained objects and creates an operational verification
608	receipt. Regeneration executes the exact retained producer and Plan input
609	closure into a candidate namespace, verifies each expected semantic identity,
610	and publishes recovered availability only if all required bytes agree. A
611	mismatch is an operational regeneration verification refusal: `HOST.IO_FAILURE`
612	(class `operational-failed`, faultCause `host-io`, exit4), domain detail
613	`evidence.regeneration-mismatch`. It cannot replace the sealed Run. New
614	source or policy creates a new Plan/Run. Expired or
615	revoked permission cannot be resurrected by a matching hash. A miss recomputes
616	normally; a corrupt hit is quarantined and disclosed before any permitted retry.
617	
618	**Constructing a cache key and admitting a hit are two different acts, and only
619	the second is an admission.** Key construction is pure and deterministic: exact
620	schema admission and canonical order over the `cache-key` record, nothing more. It
621	reads no bytes and resolves no reference, so a host may compute it before loading
622	anything and miss cheaply; it is a lookup key and grants nothing. **Finding bytes
623	under a matching key is not authority.** An entry may be consumed only against
624	exactly the closure the Run itself requires: the stage spec retained and joined to
625	this Plan, the producing closure retained and Plan-selected, every `scopeIds`
626	member a retained `subject-scope` of this snapshot, the output schema document
627	retained, and every `inputRefs` entry resolved through the same
628	`x-opensip-digest-domains` registry the Run uses — so a consumed native context
629	must be one this Plan selected, a consumed import must be one this Plan selected,
630	and nothing is admitted under a guessed payload-domain schema. A bare
631	`coverage-payload`, `import-payload` or `fact-payload` reference is refused as an
632	authoritative root rather than resolved by guesswork; those are reached only
633	through their owning object. A hit that clears all of this is reusable producer
634	output, never evidence authority, and it never replaces or re-seals a Run. The
635	same record and the same admission apply to a regeneration key; only the H domain
636	differs, and a regeneration whose result disagrees remains the
637	`evidence.regeneration-mismatch` refusal above.
638	
639	## 5. Durable custody and failure protocol
640	
641	Default `opensip`/`analyze` is DURABLE_AUTHORITATIVE under CD-RT-5. The host
642	reports retention origin DEFAULTED and durable-unbounded posture before first
643	write; the command's documented effect is admission of the project marker and
644	private registry/store, followed by an authoritative Run. No implicit policy
645	file is written. Explicit retention overrides have independent byte/time/count
646	bounds with provenance; failure to satisfy an authoritative request never
647	silently demotes it to ephemeral. `--ephemeral` is explicitly non-authoritative,
648	uses temporary custody, mints no authoritative commit receipt and cannot satisfy
649	baseline adoption, repair or authoritative replay prerequisites.
650	
651	The storage-root admission still applies the inherited sync, backup and private
652	custody classifications separately. A detected backup-managed root requires an
653	explicit storage-policy choice before the first source-derived write (TM V17):
654	select another admitted root, choose explicit ephemeral mode, or acknowledge
655	backup custody for this invocation with `--allow-backup-custody` (or the
656	corresponding already-admitted host storage-policy record). CI never prompts;
657	without that explicit choice it refuses REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED with detail
658	`storage.backup-choice-required`, before creating evidence. The acknowledgement
659	is retained as operational custody metadata; it does not alter semantic Run
660	identity or silently write a policy file. UNKNOWN backup status is disclosed as
661	unknown, never as not-backed-up. Purge never claims deletion of external copies.
662	Sync/upload roots and group/ACL exposure retain their separate admission rules;
663	a backup acknowledgement is not a network-export or shared-storage grant.
664	
665	Exactly one per-project writer holds the lifecycle lease/fence through source
666	admission, evaluation and atomic commit. Read-only clients use a consistent
667	committed ledger snapshot and never wait while holding a lock needed by the
668	writer. Global trust admission and revocation use the security contract's lock
669	order. SQLite WAL, transaction settings, fsync/atomic-rename carrier and crash
670	reconciliation retain the reviewed lifecycle carrier's native obligations;
671	the reference model here tests the semantic transition, not OS durability.
672	
673	Commit order:
674	
675	1. Validate closure and independently replay proof; compute all final IDs.
676	2. Write immutable blobs and descriptors to private temporary files, verify
677	   digest/length, fsync files, atomically publish under digest, fsync directories.
678	3. In one synchronous ledger transaction insert Run manifest, object references,
679	   retained availability generation, baseline/other authorized pins and a commit
680	   receipt with ExecutionId, namespace, monotonic sequence, inventory digest,
681	   signer and immutable assurance; commit and satisfy the carrier's barriers.
682	4. Only then acknowledge commitment. Required rendering/delivery is later and
683	   cannot rewrite the Run. Receipt signing is operational custody evidence and
684	   excluded from semantic IDs; the receipt authenticates RunId and inventory.
685	
686	A failure before step 3 publishes no authoritative Run. Orphan blobs are
687	unreferenced and eligible for GC after reconciliation. A crash after ledger
688	commit but before acknowledgement is `durability-undetermined` to the caller,
689	exit 4, with an ExecutionId for read-only recovery. Recovery checks the ledger
690	and actual objects; it returns committed or failed, never repeats a repository
691	mutation. Duplicate retry can share a Run but has a separate attempt receipt.
692	An acknowledged Run with missing/corrupt objects becomes partially available or
693	corrupt; the host does not pretend it was never sealed.
694	
695	Sealed assurance is immutable: verified means exact identity+proof checks at
696	seal; verifiable also commits the verification closure; replayable also commits
697	all exact admitted producer executables and source/input closure. The default
698	authoritative profile requires replayable retention at seal. Current
699	availability is a separate monotonic-generation record: retained, partial,
700	expired, purged, corrupt or unavailable, with exact missing references and
701	cause. Availability may improve through verified restoration or regeneration;
702	sealed assurance and historical verdict never change. A query reports both.
703	
704	Retention roots include every live Run's required closure, active baseline,
705	authorized repair prerequisite and backup/export operation pin. Automatic
706	expiry respects these pins and all independent policy bounds; it refuses a
707	new durable admission if the required closure cannot be retained within bounds.
708	A direct purge of a pinned Run refuses unless the explicit destructive purge
709	also revokes the named pins after disclosing consequences. Purge retains the
710	minimal sealed manifest, provenance and tombstone but deletes unshared evidence
711	bytes by reachability GC; shared bytes survive until the final reference is
712	removed. Purged is not deleted-history. The user may separately destroy the
713	whole project store/marker under lifecycle authorization; no indefinite privacy
714	claim is made for backups or exports already outside that store.
715	
716	A retention decision never changes a fact, Coverage, finding or Run identity.
717	It never turns expired evidence into `no match`. Query of retained manifest is
718	allowed after purge and states evidence unavailable. Query requiring actual
719	proof, comparison baseline or repair input refuses with
720	REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED and `evidence.{expired,purged,missing,corrupt}`
721	before evaluation (exit 2); inability during a selected operation is HOST.IO_FAILURE
722	with evidence detail (exit 4). Successfully admitted partial native inputs may
723	instead produce an indeterminate Run (exit 3) under the native and D9 contracts.
724	These are different event positions, not interchangeable error spellings.
725	
726	Backup/export holds a read snapshot plus short-lived object pins, writes a
727	bounded relative-path inventory, hashes and verifies every object, then seals
728	the bundle. Import checks path traversal, symlinks, sizes, duplicate paths,
729	cryptographic identities and all referenced schemas before publishing anything.
730	Source provenance/authenticity is reported separately from hash integrity.
731	Trust floors, current authorization and local custody receipts are never
732	restored backwards from an evidence backup. Portable baseline details are in
733	the workflow contract. An import cannot silently claim a remote Run was locally
734	evaluated: its imported-custody receipt names origin and local verification.
735	
736	## 6. Required implementation conformance
737	
738	Reference checks cover exact numeric and canonical encodings, wrong-source and
739	wrong-Plan joins, identity changes for each semantic input, operational identity
740	exclusion, universal negatives under incomplete resolution, proof tampering,
741	retention/purge invariance and crash acknowledgement states. They additionally
742	assert the digest law mechanically: that every 64-hex field carries a registered
743	representation, that each new closed record reproduces an independently computed
744	canonical digest vector and moves under every single-field mutation, and that a
745	complete Run with a non-empty native context set closes while an altered frame, a
746	missing preimage, a wrong preimage, an unregistered H domain, a raw payload
747	offered as an H identity and a hidden input each refuse with a typed cause. They
748	also assert that a fully re-framed and re-keyed Run built around a context the
749	native boundary refuses — contradicting honored options, a compiler or runtime
750	digest outside the tool closure, an incomplete stdlib inventory, a component
751	digest that is not the retained tree's, a compiler version not from the manifest,
752	a universe contradicting its context, or a config graph or lockfile path outside
753	the snapshot — is refused with that boundary's own typed refusal string. They
754	exercise a complete Rust universe/fact/Coverage Run alongside the TypeScript one,
755	with the nested dependency, features, config-projection and prepared-output
756	records retained and joined; and they separate cache key construction from cache
757	hit admission, showing that a key needs no bytes while a hit needs the Run's whole
758	closure. Their source pins
759	and independent review are part of D-372. They do not qualify a native carrier.
760	
761	Before shipping, the exact implementation must additionally demonstrate:
762	all supported platform fsync/SQLite/process-death cases; concurrent readers and
763	writers plus trust revocation; independent replay across machines; missing,
764	corrupt, stale and wrong-tenant closure rejection; hostile archive import; GC
765	with shared references; backup restoration preserving trust floors; and public
766	D9/CLI/JSON/SARIF/HTML/agent parity. Those are implementation acceptance criteria
767	under existing G gates, not unresolved design alternatives.
768	
769	### Reference lifecycle joins
770	
771	The reference store instantiates closed commit-receipt and availability records.
772	An availability transition increments generation and never rewrites a sealed Run
773	or its original assurance. Read-only `recover(ExecutionId)` inspects the committed
774	receipt after a lost acknowledgement and never repeats effects. Verified restoration
775	requires the same complete identity closure and replay result before availability
776	returns to retained; a regeneration mismatch refuses. Physical fsync, authenticated
777	receipt signing, shared-blob deletion and OS crash recovery remain implementation
778	qualification obligations; the reference transitions do not claim to execute them.
779	
780	The security chapter's three lease modes refine the inherited single-writer rule:
781	immutable readers coexist with the append writer; exclusive migration/purge acquires
782	the writer lease and reader exclusion. No second writer is permitted.
783	
784	At Run closure, every Plan-selected import re-admits its retained canonical SourceCorrespondence. An exact-snapshot import must name the Plan snapshot. VCS-revision imports require a retained, canonical admitted SourceMappingV1 to that snapshot, with inventory-matching source digests and the current clean revision; an unmapped/stale intake artifact may remain available for inspection but cannot be selected as an analyzed Plan input. Intake storage does not establish this source join. The authenticated importer/evaluator still owns payload-schema, observation-scope and polarity admission; rehashing an opaque import is insufficient. The reference closure reuses the same workflow import/mapping schema admission functions so the source law has one implementation.
785	
786	The semantic grant's `prepare-code` operation is present exactly when it projects trusted-repository-code preparation principals. Their provenance comes from consumed admitted host-prepared inputs; no test-runner operation or principal is added. Verification/replay checks these immutable bindings without reusing expired operational grants.
787	
788	The expected VCS build context is explicit, never inferred from the imported claim. The host may select one analysis-spec parameter whose schemaDigest is the raw SHA-256 of `foundation/import-source-context.schema.json` and whose payloadDigest binds canonical ImportSourceContextV1 `{schemaVersion:1, declaredBuildIds:[...]}`. These expected labels come from the separately admitted analysis request/build configuration; the importer cannot nominate its own expected labels. No parameter means an empty set; more than one is refused. Labels are declarations, not proof: source mapping remains mandatory. Run closure reconstructs workflow §4's binding from this retained parameter and the snapshot's VCS observation, then applies the same staleness function (both dirty flags, revision, expected build label and admitted mapping). A label not in the expected set is wrong-build and cannot become a Plan-selected import. The schema bytes and payload are retained with the Plan parameters for independent replay.
789	
790	Snapshot capture consumes the same admitted boundary inventory as native discovery. The host obtains it from successful security discovery, passes it unchanged to native discovery/membership and the shared scope descriptor, and removes nested-repository, nested-project and directory-custody-excluded paths before opening or hashing snapshot source bytes. The remaining paths are only capture candidates: per-file custody, safe handles and exact hashing still precede source admission. Boundary exclusion anchors enter the Plan's scope descriptor and their operational provenance is retained beside it. The host reference join admits one inventory; caller-supplied alternative boundary lists or substituted marker sets are refused. Discovery's dependency-tree pruning is an analysis-unit rule; explicitly required native dependency read-set bytes require separate custody/closure admission and cannot cross a nested authority boundary.
791	
792	Every Plan with selected import2 inputs also requires read-import in its semantic grant. This includes imported-inert preparation. Close_run enforces this operation/input join as well as prepare-code/principal equality; the later consuming-Plan admission separately validates the actual preparedResolution provenance.
793	
794	
795	The reference closure entry point reports a missing promised object/blob as EvidenceUnavailable carrying the closed operational-failed/HOST.IO_FAILURE/host-io termination with evidence.missing and the missing reference. It never emits a bare lookup error or turns missing witness bytes into a false predicate or admission rejection. This models the host's retained-byte/custody observation boundary. Untrusted malformed records still receive exact schema/identity admission refusal; an inventory of available retained bytes does not authorize rewriting the assurance of a sealed Run.
796

1	# Exact admission and trustworthy qualification reports
2	
3	Standing: Codex-authored successor; review and application standing is governed
4	by the [correction record](../../../coop/design-corrections/README.md) and central
5	readiness register. Addresses AR-01/02 and the G13 join to full-product native
6	and platform cells. Reference code is design evidence, not production code.
7	
8	## 1. Numeric and schema admission
9	
10	The configuration, policy and metadata carriers apply lexical admission before
11	JSON decoding can round or normalize a number. An integer field accepts an
12	ordinary integer token in its declared range. `1.0`, `1e0`, `1E0`,
13	`1.0000000000000001`, `9007199254740991.1`, booleans and numeric strings do not
14	satisfy an integer field, even if a JSON Schema implementation treats them as
15	mathematically equal. `-0`, nonfinite tokens and values outside the canonical
16	profile range are rejected. Internal configuration layers must also enforce
17	exact types; an already-decoded `1.0` or `True` cannot satisfy `const:1`.
18	
19	The [canonical reference](../../../coop/design-corrections/foundation/canonical.py)
20	provides duplicate-key, Unicode, depth, size and number admission plus an exact
21	integer/const/enum validator. Existing carrier-specific narrower bounds remain.
22	The new [foundation reference](../../../coop/design-corrections/foundation/host-foundation-model.v2.py)
23	replaces only the configuration/policy/parser entry points of
24	`completion/host-foundation-model.v1.py`. Root discovery belongs to the security
25	successor; no unsafe historical ancestor search is re-exported as current.
26	
27	Schema validation follows lexical admission and precedes configuration merge,
28	identity computation, subprocess disclosure or effects. Invalid external input
29	is an admission rejection with the existing carrier's D9 code; an invalid
30	host-generated internal layer is a host invariant fault. Unknown keys and
31	unsupported schema majors are refused. No parse fallback silently narrows a
32	user's configuration. UR-1–UR-5 are selected explicitly by the canonical profile
33	in identity-and-evidence §3, with byte vectors for non-BMP key ordering, integer
34	boundaries, Unicode normalization distinction, escaping and invalid surrogates.
35	
36	Closed identifier and digest patterns require the actual end of the string.
37	The product schemas use the portable ECMAScript assertion `(?![\s\S])` where
38	an end anchor is intended, because `$` can also match before a final newline.
39	A newline-suffixed identifier or digest is malformed; stripping whitespace is
40	not an admission repair. Canonical string encoding itself continues to preserve
41	legal scalar characters, including escaped newlines in ordinary text fields.
42	
43	### 1.1 Full-product configuration and zero-config defaults
44	
45	The historical numeric regression adapter deliberately retains the preview's
46	compiled profile. Full-product configuration instead uses
47	`foundation/product-configuration.schema.v2.json` and its resolution reference.
48	It has closed optional sections: analysis (registered profile/capabilities and
49	work budget), components (existing request/pins/holds/scope selection), discovery
50	(entryPoints/workspaceRoots/ignorePaths), policy (registered pack/waiver IDs),
51	evidence (already-admitted import2 IDs), retention (independent nullable positive
52	byte/Run/age bounds), and UI color. Every file declares schemaVersion=2. No
53	configuration field executes code, imports ambient evidence, grants permission,
54	selects an unregistered capability or rewrites a policy file.
55	
56	The authenticated release declaration registry supplies the `default` profile
57	and exact applicable TS/JS/Rust capabilities; it is not the old
58	`preview-typescript` constant. Discovery populates compiled default values with
59	recognizer/evidence provenance. Then global, project, interactive local and
60	explicit flags override in order; arrays replace atomically and records merge
61	by named field. The environment semantic layer remains empty. CI never probes
62	the interactive local carrier. Technical recognition is input evidence feeding
63	default selection, not an authority layer that can override explicit intent.
64	Winning value, source layer and discovery evidence remain explainable.
65	
66	Entry/workspace/ignore paths are bounded canonical project-relative paths;
67	`.` is the sole project-root sentinel for workspaceRoots and ignorePaths;
68	entryPoints names a concrete source path and cannot use the root sentinel.
69	Omitting workspaceRoots selects automatic discovery; an explicitly supplied
70	workspaceRoots array must be nonempty. `[]` is refused rather than silently
71	interpreted as automatic discovery or as a different native unit selection.
72	ignorePaths removes that exact path and descendants by whole path segment,
73	not arbitrary substring. Explicit roots/entries are validated against the
74	admitted repository boundary and selected language mode; an absent selected
75	path is CONFIG.INVALID, never silently dropped. An explicit empty entry list
76	is retained and results in honest incomplete reachability. Native recognizers
77	own richer discovered test globs and framework semantics; these three override
78	fields do not execute a glob language. Unknown registry IDs and conflicting
79	component pins/holds refuse before Plan construction under the deterministic
80	component resolver. Already-imported evidence IDs must belong to the admitted
81	project/source/build context under the native/workflow import contract.
82	
83	Resolved semantic configuration contains analysis, components, discovery,
84	policy and evidence values: **all five sections are always present** in the
85	resolved semantic record; a section with no selected fields is exactly `{}`.
86	An empty section is never omitted. `analysis` always contains `profileId`,
87	`capabilities` and the complete `{unit,limit}` budget supplied by the authenticated
88	compiled defaults and then overridden by admitted layers. Missing profile refuses
89	`CONFIG_PROFILE_MISSING`; missing compiled capabilities/budget is the internal
90	resolver invariant `CONFIG_DEFAULTS_INCOMPLETE`, never a second zero-config spelling.
91	Other section fields are present exactly when selected by default/discovery or an
92	explicit layer; no implicit empty list is inserted. Thus absent entryPoints means
93	automatic recognition while explicit `[]` remains deliberate empty intent.
94	The post-resolution shape is closed by identity-schemas.v2's
95	`semantic-configuration`, distinct from the optional input-layer schema.
96	Every array in the input-layer schema explicitly declares `sequence`: layer
97	admission preserves the user's input until resolution. This is distinct from
98	the resolved schema's canonical-set annotations; schema admission never performs
99	the resolver's normalization. All current native, security and workflow schema
100	arrays likewise declare their owning order using identity §3's enforced keyword.
101	Sets sort by canonical item bytes; allowedScopes
102	retains its declared project-before-global priority order. Its digest is SHA256
103	of canonical semantic configuration bytes. UI, retention bounds, transport
104	presentation and custody acknowledgements remain operational and cannot alter
105	that digest; their actual policy/admission still applies. Semantic discovery and
106	native context digests bind recognizer versions and meaningful effects to Plan.
107	Configuration-carrier provenance is retained separately from source-code blobs;
108	a presentation-only CLI change cannot affect Snapshot/Plan/Run.
109	
110	Schema-one project/global/local files may be read only through the exact legacy
111	schema and lexical admission, then explicitly projected in memory to the common
112	version-two fields with sourceSchemaVersion=1 provenance. No file is rewritten
113	implicitly and no new grant is inferred. Unsupported legacy fields refuse.
114	Compiled preview defaults are never used as product defaults. A requested
115	configuration migration is a reviewable data patch through the workflow's
116	configuration-write authorization, not a side effect of analysis.
117	
118	`check-product-configuration.py` retains no-config mixed-native selection,
119	explicit-entry override, exact schema numbers, unknown capability/path refusal,
120	CI local non-consumption and semantic-versus-operational digest cases. Actual
121	framework/custody/component resolution has its own native/security/lifecycle
122	conformance; this narrow resolver does not claim to implement those adapters.
123	
124	## 2. Separate report custody, semantic correctness and qualification
125	
126	The release gate has an authenticated invocation context before reading a
127	candidate report: exact host, provider/data closure, harness, matrix, corpus,
128	runner public key, runner identity, environment observation and platform profile.
129	The fresh qualificationRequestId (host RequestId grammar) also binds the
130	measurement campaign; an older report cannot satisfy a different campaign.
131	These come from the selected signed release closure and independently admitted
132	runner inventory. A report cannot supply or alter its own expected subject,
133	expected answers, trusted runner or performance baseline.
134	
135	The producer signs the exact report bytes through the qualification signature
136	frame: ASCII `opensip.qualification.report.2`, NUL, raw 32-byte host digest,
137	provider-closure digest, harness digest, and SHA256(report bytes), concatenated
138	in that order. Ed25519 keys are provisioned by the authenticated gate outside
139	the report. The gate verifies signature before parsing bounded report bytes.
140	The report's embedded schemaMajor is covered by the signature. Reusing this
141	signature frame for report schema 3 does not make schema 2 bytes schema 3.
142	
143	Authentication proves who supplied the observation; it does not prove the
144	machine executed correctly. The trusted first-party measurement harness,
145	runner observation path and gate are explicit TCB components. The harness must
146	execute the selected closure by verified handle, observe exit/EOF and normalized
147	actual results, and bind the exact measured environment. Product qualification
148	requires retained real measurements from every required lane; synthetic reports
149	are tagged reference-only and cannot be promoted. A producer cannot attest its
150	own unsupported hardware into the allowlist.
151	
152	The original G13 schema/validator remain frozen historical evidence. The new
153	`g13-result-schema.v5.json` and `g13-validator.v5.py` close the reproduced defects
154	for the historical 24-cell shape: independently pinned corpus oracles determine
155	expected atoms and counters, all subject digests join to trusted context, and
156	actual observations plus signature are required. Consistently relabeling every
157	candidate subject digest or zeroing both expected and actual counts now fails.
158	This adapter does not qualify the added JavaScript/Rust cells.
159	
160	## 3. Full-product matrix and report schema
161	
162	The current native matrix is
163	`native/native-capability-matrix.v2.json`. Expand each declared capability/mode
164	cell over its four platform families and each selected signed platform profile
165	from the security contract. A release inventory explicitly selects the
166	advertised supported cells; unsupported typed cells also receive refusal
167	conformance cases. No cell disappears because no runner happened to produce a
168	report. Syntax-only capability is further parameterized by the exact grammar
169	inventory; one grammar's result does not qualify another grammar.
170	
171	The full-product report schema is
172	`foundation/product-quality-report.schema.v3.json`; its gate reference is
173	`foundation/product-quality-validator.py`. A report covers exactly one trusted
174	runner/profile/environment and the required cell set for that lane. CellId is
175	`capability/mode/platform/profile/fixture`; each coordinate comes from the
176	reviewed matrix and corpus expansion, not from report labels. Every required
177	fixture names exact source/input bytes, selected capability/rung, expected
178	normalized observations, expected exit and independently chosen work/stress
179	bounds. Native reference scenarios supply semantic obligations; executable
180	native fixtures and their results must be admitted at implementation
181	qualification before a cell becomes QUALIFIED.
182	
183	The gate's expectedCells is constructed from the verified matrix/corpus and
184	release selection by the first-party gate. It cannot be supplied as a CLI JSON
185	argument, copied out of report fields or recomputed from candidate answers.
186	Expected observation atoms have closed fields `kind`, `subject`, `value` (all
187	strings); `value` is the schema-defined normalized scalar or canonical JSON
188	text for structured payloads. The admitted fixture's normalizer and schema
189	are part of its pinned harness closure. Report atoms sort by canonical bytes,
190	are unique, and must equal the independent oracle exactly. Counts and
191	correctness are calculated by the gate; they are absent from the submitted
192	schema. Duplicate cells/observations, wrong cell sets, wrong exit or substituted
193	answers cannot be hidden by a reported PASS flag because no such flag is read.
194	
195	Each benchmark records 3 warmups followed by 7 measured runs in that order,
196	with positive integer elapsed nanoseconds and peak RSS bytes. The gate calculates median
197	elapsed time and maximum RSS. For an existing baseline the limits are 1.20×
198	median time and 1.25× peak RSS, using checked wide-integer cross multiplication (never wrapping), plus the
199	fixture's independently reviewed absolute bounds. A new supported cell needs
200	an explicitly reviewed initial baseline and absolute budget; absence is not a
201	zero or automatic pass. The two baseline measurements must be both present
202	or both null. A null pair admits an initial-measurement report but never qualifies
203	a release-selected cell; reviewed initial baseline promotion is a separate gate act. Baseline host/provider/harness, fixture, environment and
204	platform profile must be compatible by the release gate's signed inventory;
205	changing the measuring subject cannot silently reuse an unrelated baseline.
206	Cold-start and retained-evidence workloads are separate fixtures, so warmup
207	cannot conceal startup or storage regressions. The old reference adapter
208	retains its historical hardware/performance baseline semantics unchanged.
209	
210	A well-formed authenticated report may report a failing observation. Report
211	admission and release qualification are separate: admission verifies custody,
212	shape and joins; qualification requires every selected cell's correctness and
213	performance to pass on every required profile lane. Missing, unavailable or
214	failed lanes block promotion. The release gate also requires lifecycle,
215	security, output parity and recovery gates; G13 alone never authorizes release.
216	
217	## 4. Reference evidence and implementation obligations
218	
219	`foundation/check-foundation.py` retains the original integer and G13
220	counterexamples, valid controls, exact canonical byte vectors and actual
221	Ed25519 signature verification with temporary test keys. The reference invokes
222	the local OpenSSL executable solely to exercise cryptography; production uses
223	the authenticated first-party implementation, never ambient tool discovery.
224	`foundation/check-identity.py` independently replays a bounded finite-relation
225	fixture and exercises identity, proof tampering, retention and crash-state
226	joins. It explicitly discloses its trusted evaluator callback and in-memory
227	carrier scope; it is not a general native interpreter or a durability proof.
228	The full-product report checks exercise a separate TS/JS/Rust-shaped cell set,
229	forged subject/corpus/answers, missing lanes and false performance claims.
230	
231	Reports record every scenario, source pins and limits. Independent review reads
232	semantics and executes adversarial controls; source hashes establish the
233	reviewed bytes, not correctness. Legacy self-reporting checker claims and their
234	observability escapes do not enter product evaluation authority. The corrected
235	product uses explicit admitted data plus trusted pure evaluation; an adversarial
236	program sharing the verifier's process is not claimed to be contained by Python
237	introspection. Native measurements, independent implementer reproduction and
238	supported-platform qualification remain the concrete pre-release gates.
239	
240	Discovery observations are folded into the trusted `defaults` layer by the host
241	before the reference Config2 resolver runs; their recognizer identity and path
242	provenance remain in the discovery record. The reference resolver does not scan
243	frameworks. A missing profile is `CONFIG_PROFILE_MISSING`; an unknown profile is
244	`CONFIG_PROFILE_UNREGISTERED`. Both pack and waiver IDs require registry admission.
245	
246	## 5. Complete product-boundary successor (DR-117)
247	
248	D-371/D-372 prospectively replace P-1/P-2/G3 only as enumerated here. These are the seven dispositions required by architecture file02, “Current V1 product boundary and required successors”; the historical enumeration and preview acceptance keep their original scope.
249	
250	1. **Marketplace/catalog and governance depth:** the selected product has one signed first-party component/recipe/schema registry. It has no public marketplace, third-party publisher admission or ecosystem governance promise. Unknown contributions refuse through the closed registry; declaring an id does not establish trust.
251	2. **External lifecycle parity and discovery:** supported first-party components receive the common installation, update, rollback, offline, doctor and removal contracts. Repository/framework discovery selects applicable admitted capabilities; it is not an external service and cannot install or execute discovered code. Third-party lifecycle parity is outside the selected scope, not a partially specified admission mode.
252	3. **Contribution roles beyond narrow/data-only:** first-party native providers may produce typed facts/Coverage and prepared input imports. Signed first-party declarative recipes/profiles may select host-owned steps. Only the host constructs findings, evaluates policy/verdict, owns persistence, finalization, rendering and termination. A component cannot acquire those powers by declaring a root command or emitting an output record.
253	4. **Untrusted native or WASM admission and enforcement:** neither is admitted in this product. No process/WASM boundary is claimed as a sandbox. Separately authorized repository-code preparation/tests are the explicit trusted-code principal of security S10, with the actual platform disclosure/enforcement matrix and revocation/cleanup rules. They do not open an untrusted plugin admission path. G09/G21/G29/G30 must exercise these refusal and authority boundaries; a synthetic fixture is not enforcement evidence.
254	5. **Imperative contributions, probes, project hooks and root commands:** arbitrary imperative contributions/project hooks/root-parser extensions are not admitted. The closed host command inventory owns every command. Named first-party repair, test, preparation and doctor operations have their exact explicit authorization and effect contracts; a recipe/profile cannot bypass them. Metadata discovery/help/recommend do not run repository hooks or probes. Consent to one executable step never becomes general command or persistence authority.
255	6. **Network-granted analysis and egress defaults:** ordinary analysis/discovery are offline; there is no implicit index refresh, download, telemetry or required egress. Explicit trust refresh/offline import and explicitly required export delivery have their named host lifecycle/output semantics. Repository-code effects are disclosed/admitted by their actual trusted-code grant; they are never silently reclassified as confined analysis. Required delivery failure can fail the invocation without changing a committed Run's assurance.
256	7. **G3 physical substrate:** the selected substrate is a signed Rust distribution core/semantic host, pure first-party evaluator, supervised native TS/JS and Rust components, and the signed offline assets and verified storage mechanics required for the selected authoritative profile. This replaces the prototype's lockstep Node/npm train and the preview's narrow command/provider set. The default product profile is authoritative-capable; an explicitly selected management-only installation is not an authoritative closure and refuses analysis until the required signed closure is separately installed through an authorized lifecycle operation. Missing assets never trigger ambient downloads or a weaker analyzer. Every physical dependency, including compiler/runtime/standard-library/LLVM/storage assets actually used, belongs to the admitted closure/TCB inventory and its packaging/offline/quality gates.
257	
258	The selected exclusions are D-371's credentials, third-party ecosystem, untrusted contributions and TUI exclusions; this section introduces no new scope cut. Product measurements remain required by the named release gates. This is a complete boundary selection now, not a promise that future implementation will choose these policies.
259

1	# Evidence workflows and product contracts
2	
3	**Standing:** Acceptance, exact reviewed bytes, and reversibility are recorded
4	in [D-370](../../coop/COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md#d-370--fallow-informed-product-design).
5	**Scope:** Design constraints settled before implementation; the D-369 preview
6	remains the selected implementation scope. This chapter adds no executable
7	capability, public command, wire field, identity recipe, or release qualification.
8	
9	The [Fallow borrow register](../../coop/FALLOW-BORROW-REGISTER.md) maps the
10	original seven ideas and eight further observations to their sources and these
11	decisions. Fallow is design evidence, not a dependency or an authority over
12	OpenSIP semantics.
13	
14	## 1. Scope and ownership
15	
16	OpenSIP's product remains an evidence compiler with one host. Providers supply
17	declared facts and Coverage; rules declare predicates and evidence requirements;
18	the pure evaluator computes policy results; the host owns admission, identity,
19	configuration, supervision, and projections. Model-assisted exploration and
20	external review remain advisory under the [Map/Control boundary](../../MAP-VS-CONTROL.md).
21	No model call or external judgment becomes a required input to Control.
22	
23	These commitments refine that architecture in two ways:
24	
25	- **Preview implementation guidance** explains existing obligations: explicit
26	  insufficiency, consistent human/JSON meaning, deterministic declared inputs,
27	  host-owned common behavior, and refusal of unsupported operations. It changes
28	  no preview schema, threshold, supported platform, required gate, or row grade.
29	- **Future capability constraints** settle ownership, evidence handoffs, and
30	  failure semantics now. Before a future capability enters a supported slice,
31	  its owning register rows must accept the concrete schemas, identity and
32	  lifecycle joins, fixtures, resource limits, and product scope it needs.
33	
34	The [reference handoff](../../coop/completion/reference-architecture.v2.md)
35	continues to own the exact preview: `analyze`, `doctor`, help/version, one
36	TypeScript provider, and the bundled import-cycle rule. This chapter does not
37	enable a baseline, repair, review, discovery command, additional rule pack,
38	runtime importer, semantic-similarity model, durable result cache, or Map.
39	Existing admission must continue to refuse excluded forms. A future feature is
40	not implemented by reserving an undocumented flag or accepting an open payload.
41	
42	## 2. Discovery and zero-config behavior
43	
44	For each supported conventional project shape, the product goal is useful
45	analysis without requiring a user-authored OpenSIP configuration. An installed,
46	compatible analysis closure is a prerequisite; zero-config is not permission to
47	download tools, execute repository configuration, or grant effects implicitly.
48	
49	Discovery distinguishes three kinds of information:
50	
51	| Information | Owner and treatment |
52	|---|---|
53	| Observed technical facts: language, manifest, workspace layout, recognized convention | Discovery producer reports the source and uncertainty; the host validates and resolves applicability. |
54	| Product defaults: supported ignore conventions and default profile selection | Host-owned, versioned, disclosed, and overridable through existing configuration precedence. |
55	| Project decisions: gate strictness, allowed dependencies, waivers, boundary intent | Explicit project policy; a detector or recommender cannot adopt these on the project's behalf. |
56	
57	Any discovered value that affects analysis must enter the ordinary declared
58	input/resolution path with provenance. There is no seventh configuration layer,
59	provider-private override, or hidden environment input. An explicit supported
60	override wins according to the existing resolver; ambiguity is disclosed rather
61	than silently selecting a broader or weaker interpretation. Ignored and
62	unsupported regions are scope information, never evidence that those regions
63	are clean.
64	
65	A future recommendation surface returns detected evidence, proposed settings,
66	default rationale, unresolved choices, and the effect of each choice. Reading a
67	recommendation does not write configuration. Applying it is a separate host
68	operation with the normal write authority. Proposed settings must be accepted
69	by the actual strict configuration resolver, not merely validate against a
70	JSON Schema; schema references must resolve from the supported offline closure.
71	The preview's read-only `doctor`
72	does not become a source analyzer or execute configuration to make detection
73	more convenient.
74	
75	Qualification for newly supported project conventions should use pinned real
76	repository shapes and nearby negative cases, including generated sources,
77	monorepo consumers, and convention-loaded entry points. Record how many manual
78	corrections are needed for a useful result and which gaps remain. Repeated
79	workarounds are investigation inputs, not automatically confirmed bugs or
80	permission to collect private repositories. Exact corpus and numeric targets
81	belong to the capability's later qualification decision; no target is invented
82	here.
83	
84	## 3. Evidence sufficiency and visible omissions
85	
86	Preserve C-1: evidence is sufficient for a particular predicate over a declared
87	scope. Syntax, resolved symbols, tests, runtime observations, and repository
88	history do not form one global strength or confidence ranking. Independent
89	evidence may support different claims about the same subject without being
90	collapsed into a single score.
91	
92	Every supported assessment projection must preserve the distinction between:
93	
94	- completed analysis with no matches in the admitted scope;
95	- unsupported, disabled, or inapplicable analysis; and
96	- attempted analysis with missing, failed, truncated, or insufficient evidence.
97	
98	These are semantic distinctions, not new wire-enum spellings. Existing typed
99	Coverage and diagnostics carry preview meaning. Future schemas must retain the
100	selected scope, applicable requirements, omissions and reasons, and truncation
101	or completion information needed to interpret the result. A count is meaningful
102	only together with that scope and sufficiency. Cancelling or exhausting a
103	budget cannot produce a clean result from a truncated subject set.
104	
105	Optional evidence can be absent while independently sufficient predicates still
106	complete. A predicate whose required evidence is missing remains indeterminate;
107	reporting other completed predicates cannot make it pass. A syntactic fact may
108	satisfy a syntactic predicate, but cannot substitute for required semantic
109	resolution. A summary or renderer must not erase this distinction.
110	
111	## 4. Candidate, inspection, and review handoffs
112	
113	Future advisory discovery separates observations from judgments. A candidate
114	means that investigation is warranted; it is neither a proven finding nor a
115	policy outcome. Deterministic clone detection describes exact or normalized
116	structure under a named algorithm. Model-based similarity remains a separate
117	Map capability: a score is model-specific and does not prove behavioral
118	equivalence or refactor safety. This separation replaces the proposed single
119	progression from exact clones to supposedly stronger semantic confidence.
120	
121	An inspection request selects an exact candidate from an explicit discovery
122	result. Its handoff binds the project, source subjects with their content
123	identity (the sealed Snapshot or per-subject content digests), scope,
124	producer/schema versions, relevant parameters, and completion information. Inspection either
125	uses retained source evidence or validates the currently opened source against
126	that handoff. Stale, missing, ambiguous, or outside-scope subjects are reported
127	explicitly. It cannot silently rerun retrieval and substitute a new candidate.
128	
129	External reviews remain separate artifacts referencing the reviewed result and
130	subject binding. A later review-join operation validates supported versions,
131	membership, duplicate judgments, and source correspondence. Unreviewed
132	candidates remain visible; requiring every candidate to be reviewed is an
133	explicit workflow condition. Matching an identifier validates correlation, not
134	the truth of an agent's prose. Missing or contradictory evidence permits
135	abstention.
136	
137	An advisory item claiming to cite Control must reference an actual host-emitted
138	item in its named view; unknown references are rejected. Map may also produce
139	its own labeled observations or hypotheses under its separate contract. Those
140	do not become Control citations merely because they mention the same file.
141	
142	Keep three questions independent: whether the candidate merits investigation,
143	whether the compared behavior is equivalent, and whether a proposed refactor is
144	safe in context. A favorable similarity score answers none of them by itself.
145	No external verdict edits the original observations or directly changes a
146	Control result, waiver, baseline, or exit. Any supported future human policy
147	action must use its own host-owned policy path.
148	
149	These are required binding dimensions, not new durable identifier recipes.
150	Candidate and review identities, retained source policy, and review storage must
151	be designed under the owning future contracts. Preview correlation identifiers
152	must not be advertised as stable finding identities or sealed Runs.
153	
154	## 5. Remediation requires its own evidence
155	
156	A future repair recipe declares the action, exact target binding, evidence
157	requirements, permitted edit scope, and verification obligations. Reporting a
158	candidate does not make its removal safe. "No references in the checked scope"
159	is distinct from "no possible consumers"; unresolved owning projects, dynamic
160	dispatch, external consumers, or incomplete runtime observation remain explicit
161	limitations relevant to the particular repair.
162	
163	The repair lifecycle has separate preview and apply operations. A preview
164	describes edits and unmet preconditions without changing source. Apply checks
165	current source identity, current authorization, and evidence sufficiency at the
166	mutation boundary. A source change or evidence mismatch invalidates the plan;
167	the host refuses it and requires a new preview instead of relocating an edit
168	heuristically. A component cannot mutate source independently of the host.
169	
170	Verification runs against the resulting source through ordinary analysis and
171	any declared, separately authorized tests. An applied edit and a verified
172	outcome are distinct results. Failed verification cannot be presented as a
173	successful repair. Multi-file atomicity, interruption, partial edits, rollback
174	ownership, and exact verification outcomes must be closed in the repair
175	contract before apply is supported. This chapter does not select a filesystem
176	transaction algorithm or authorize a test runner in the preview.
177	
178	## 6. Delta attribution and policy changes
179	
180	Preserve the existing versioned fingerprint and detector-pivot architecture.
181	A finding difference alone cannot establish a code regression when the
182	detector, rule selection, parameters, scope, required evidence, or policy also
183	changed. Baseline adoption remains an explicit host-owned policy operation.
184	
185	A future comparison identifies both source snapshots and both analysis/policy
186	contexts. It separates code-introduced or code-fixed results from detector
187	changes, policy changes, scope changes, waivers, and changes in evidence
188	availability. Use controlled comparisons under compatible semantics to make an
189	attribution; otherwise report the affected comparison as indeterminate. Do not
190	rename an unclassifiable result "inherited" or count a vanished finding as fixed
191	merely because its rule was disabled or its file ignored.
192	
193	The report/gate scope is distinct from the fact derivation scope. A PR may gate
194	only introduced findings while analysis still requires unchanged consumers,
195	entry points, dependencies, or test relationships. Restricting output to changed
196	lines does not establish a complete graph over just those lines. Supplied diff
197	scope and comparison base must agree or be reported incompatible; clone-group
198	reshaping alone does not prove new duplicated code was written.
199	
200	Policy deltas should use schema-aware semantics: raising a maximum allowed
201	complexity weakens it, while lowering a minimum coverage weakens that policy.
202	String matching or the direction of a number alone is not an enforcement rule.
203	The host projects tracked policy changes; new/removed/skipped tests and removed
204	CI steps may also be advisory review observations with stated detection limits.
205	
206	Metrics are reported with their population and unit. A smaller worst function,
207	more functions, and unchanged branching may describe decomposition, which can
208	improve readability without removing decisions. Do not claim behavioral
209	simplification from that metric alone. A suppression changes handling of a
210	finding, not the measured source property. Future waiver/suppression inventory
211	should expose rationale, scope, and staleness using the owning policy contract.
212	
213	## 7. Runtime, test, and history evidence
214	
215	Future evidence import is explicit, bounded, and local-first. Collection or
216	network retrieval is a separate capability and authority decision; analyzing a
217	repository does not implicitly execute tests or start production monitoring.
218	
219	Runtime evidence must state source/build correspondence, capture provenance,
220	observation window, observed population, mapping gaps, and which subjects were
221	observable. Distinguish observed execution, observable-but-unhit code, and code
222	the capture could not observe. An unmatched build or missing source map cannot
223	be treated as an unhit function. A test coverage artifact does not establish
224	production traffic, and an absence of hits during one window does not prove
225	code is safe to delete.
226	
227	Tests and history similarly retain source correspondence, collection scope,
228	tool/version provenance where relevant, and limitations. An impact-selected
229	test list is a bounded recommendation unless the evidence establishes the
230	claimed selection completeness. History or runtime importance may guide
231	advisory review priority; any future deterministic policy over these inputs
232	requires a separately admitted artifact and a declared predicate. Evidence
233	conflicts and gaps remain visible rather than being averaged into confidence.
234	
235	Runtime execution coverage is distinct from OpenSIP Coverage, which describes
236	analysis sufficiency. Freshness, retention, artifact admission, data privacy,
237	and exact source-map/build binding require concrete future contracts. The
238	preview's SC-CACHE/SC-OPS/SC-TRUST state selection is unchanged; no runtime or
239	review evidence store is smuggled into an operational cache.
240	
241	## 8. Common contracts and evidence reuse
242	
243	Implement common behavior from one host-owned declaration registry or generated
244	contract source, with drift checks against the actual supported operations and
245	schemas. Public inventories should describe rules/capabilities, accepted input
246	and output schemas, applicability, supported projections, stable diagnostic
247	codes, and action availability from their owning contracts. The exact signed
248	component schema remains its existing owner; this registry neither adds an
249	unsigned capability claim nor creates a plugin ABI.
250	
251	Rule/contribution updates cannot silently select project policy, introduce a
252	private configuration precedence, or change gate behavior through recommended
253	defaults. Host admission validates declarations even if a component uses the
254	SDK. Independent release compatibility remains per surface; generated artifacts
255	must not force all components onto one release version.
256	
257	Generate or drift-check factual help/schema/adapter inventories from the same
258	source. Keep audience-specific explanation separate, but flag it for review when
259	its underlying contract changes. Tests must cover supported human/JSON
260	semantics in the preview and each additional adapter when advertised; a core
261	test alone does not demonstrate that an adapter preserves the result.
262	
263	Report formatting consumes an explicit typed assessment; it does not crawl the
264	working tree, run an analyzer, read physical tables, or recompute findings.
265	Expensive facts can be shared within a valid analysis operation. Future saved
266	reports and inspection surfaces use the common typed query boundary and disclose
267	unavailable retained evidence instead of reconstructing it invisibly. Source
268	enrichment is an explicit inspection operation, not a renderer side effect.
269	Cross-run result reuse remains excluded from the preview. Exact acceleration
270	and semantic production retain the distinction in the Gortex borrow register.
271	
272	## 9. Coherent workflows and bounded review
273	
274	Preserve one host invocation containing typed steps. A named workflow is data
275	selecting existing host-owned operations, not a peer tool with private policy,
276	persistence, command hooks, or exits. Step requirements and dependencies must be
277	explicit; aggregation cannot hide a failed or indeterminate required step.
278	The existing Plan/workflow contracts own exact identity, cancellation, outcome,
279	and future parent/child links. No extra Invocation or Run identity is defined
280	here, and the preview is still the single supported analysis path.
281	
282	A future review brief and target inspection compose existing evidence. The
283	brief may prioritize boundary crossings, public contract changes, dependency
284	changes, consumers outside the diff, and test/runtime/history context when
285	available. Deterministic selection records its version, inputs, reasons, scope,
286	limits, and omissions. A bounded top list is a view over findings, never a
287	policy truncation: omitted findings still participate in their ordinary gate.
288	Any agent framing remains separately identified and advisory. User research and
289	measurements should choose the list size; Fallow's three-to-five limit is not
290	adopted as an OpenSIP constant.
291	
292	## 10. Declarative policy authoring
293	
294	Future policy authoring should supply schema guidance, rule explanations,
295	positive and negative examples, and an explicit preview/test operation before
296	enforcement. Preview reports the effective policy and proposed change; it does
297	not rewrite tracked intent or promote a rule's severity implicitly. Test
298	overrides must be disclosed and scoped to that invocation.
299	
300	Packs remain data-only contributions evaluated under host authority. A rule
301	such as "this layer does not perform network access" must distinguish a ban on
302	known direct calls from a transitive absence-of-effects claim. The latter needs
303	appropriate semantic relations and complete scope; an unknown callee is not
304	evidence of purity. No effect catalogue from another analyzer is accepted as
305	universal effect semantics.
306	
307	The preview accepts only its bundled cycle pack. External packs, additional
308	rules, pack-test commands, and admission of user-authored policies retain their
309	existing scope re-entry requirements.
310	
311	## 11. Integration and future acceptance
312	
313	The architectural decisions in sections 2–10 are settled here; exact public
314	schemas and algorithms for excluded capabilities are not represented as
315	implementation-ready. Their scope admission must satisfy these constraints and
316	the owning rows in the [central readiness register](08-decision-and-readiness-register.md):
317	
318	| Design area | Existing ownership to revisit when scope enters |
319	|---|---|
320	| Discovery, defaults, common declaration registry | DR-103, DR-117, DR-120, DR-123, DR-125; language applicability DR-118 |
321	| Sufficiency, native facts, richer evidence | DR-004, DR-005, DR-118, DR-133; runtime effects/security DR-105/117 |
322	| Candidates, review, runtime retention, repair | DR-002, DR-006–009, DR-105, DR-117; Map boundary and state ownership DR-109/124 |
323	| Baseline and policy attribution | DR-002, DR-006–008, DR-011, DR-111; policy provenance DR-103 |
324	| Workflow, projections, rule-authoring surfaces | DR-117, DR-122/123/125, DR-131; future pack admission under the product boundary |
325	
326	This is an ownership map, not another readiness checklist. No row is closed or
327	regraded here. File 08 and its D-369 after-image remain unchanged because the
328	preview's accepted behavior and gates are unchanged. The decision register and
329	current reading path link this supplement now, before implementation begins.
330	
331	Future qualification must exercise the actual capability input path, including
332	unknown/partial evidence, source changes between review and apply, invalid
333	review membership, policy-only changes, incompatible comparisons, and bounded
334	output. Those are acceptance obligations for the future capability, not claims
335	that newly authored product fixtures or passing runtime tests exist today.

91	### 1.1 Cell coordinates

106	### 1.2 Language modes (closed)
107	
108	| Mode id | Recognition | Universe | Notes |
109	|---|---|---|---|
110	| `ts-tsconfig` | `tsconfig.json` at the unit root (or named by discovery), `allowJs` absent/false | `typescript-v2`, `configOrigin=tsconfig` | JavaScript files are not program roots; a JS import target is `unresolved-module-specifier`. |
111	| `js-allowjs` | `tsconfig.json`/`jsconfig.json` with effective `allowJs=true` (jsconfig defaults `allowJs=true`) | `typescript-v2`, `allowJs=true` | `.js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx` are program roots. |
112	| `js-synthesized` | No `tsconfig.json`/`jsconfig.json` at the unit root; `package.json` present or any `.js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx` file under the unit | `typescript-v2`, `configOrigin=synthesized`, `synthesizerVersion=1` | Host synthesizes `SynthesizedCompilerOptionsV1` (§2.2); Plan-bound with `DEFAULTED` provenance, disclosed in output. |
113	| `rust-cargo` | `Cargo.toml` at the unit root (package or workspace) | `rust-v2` | Requires a sealed `DependencySourceSetV1` when the lock lists any non-path package (§3). |
114	| `rust-cargo-prepared` | as above, plus an admitted `PreparedOutputSetV3` of inert rows | `rust-v2` with `preparedOutputSetId` non-null | Expansions and directives are consumed as data; a site without a row is an unresolved edge (§3.6). |

116	
117	**`allowJs` and `checkJs` are not completeness claims** (feedback 11; primary
118	sources `typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/allowJs` and `/checkJs`, read 2026-09-06).
119	`allowJs` is a *program-membership* option: it admits JavaScript roots. `checkJs`
120	is a *diagnostics* option: it reports errors in JavaScript files and changes
121	nothing about what is resolved. Both are universe keys (they change PlanId);
122	neither gates a capability, and neither implies that resolution was attempted or
123	complete. Resolution completeness is asserted only by `CoverageResultV3` (§4.3).
124	The universe carries `jsAdmittedToProgram`, `jsDiagnosticsEnabled` and the
125	constant `resolutionCompletenessImplied=false` so no consumer can confuse them.

128	and `require()`/`module.exports` are both resolved by the pinned compiler under
129	`module=node16` semantics keyed by `package.json` `type`. A non-literal specifier
130	is an unresolved edge (§4.4), never a silent drop.

151	TypeScript `references`/`calls` carry L-JS2 as well: computed member access,
152	`any`-typed calls and structural dispatch exist in TypeScript programs, not only
153	in JavaScript. The v1 draft's `✓` for those cells was wrong.

155	Limitations (closed ids; each is disclosed in Coverage, never hidden):
156	
157	- **L-JS1** synthesized options: `paths`/`baseUrl`/`rootDirs`/custom `types` are unknown; a specifier resolvable only through them is `unresolved-module-specifier`.
158	- **L-JS2** dynamic forms: computed member access, non-literal `require`/`import()`, indirect `eval`, reflective access and `any`-typed calls produce unresolved edges; resolution completeness for universal negatives is then `incomplete` (§4).
159	- **L-JS3** JavaScript types without annotation or JSDoc are `compiler-inferred` (§4.8). They are exact under the admitted universe and carry no probabilistic confidence; a rule pack that wants declared types uses `derivationPolicy=declared-only`.
160	- **L-RS1** external crates: every non-path package in `Cargo.lock` that unified feature resolution activates for the target must be present in the sealed dependency source set; otherwise the dependent crate's semantic rungs are `input-closure-incomplete` (§3.5). Syntax rungs remain complete.
161	- **L-RS2** dynamic dispatch and generics: `dyn Trait` calls resolve to the trait method declaration and are recorded as `trait-object-dynamic-dispatch` unresolved edges; generic bound calls as `generic-bound-dispatch`. Both count against resolution completeness for universal negatives.
162	- **L-RS3** non-prepared generated code: procedural-macro and build-script outputs are absent; each external proc-macro invocation site is a `macro-expansion-unavailable` edge and each package with a build script contributes `build-script-generated-unavailable`. `types@checked` on items whose type depends on such generated code is `unknown` with `input-closure-incomplete` (cause `generated-output-unavailable`). Declarative `macro_rules!` expansion is compiler-native and fully supported.
163	- **L-RS4** prepared mode: only inert `macro-expansion`, `build-script-directives` and `generated-file` rows are consumed (the last through the read-only virtual `OUT_DIR`, §3.6 PO-4); a site or owner without a matching, non-stale row falls back to L-RS3 behavior for that site.
164	- **L-FW1** entry points: `reachability` universal negatives need an origin set; without a recognized framework or explicit origins they are `resolution-incomplete` with class `entry-point-unrecognized` (§8).
165	- **L-CL1** cross-TS/JS candidates use the `tsjs-erasure-v1` syntax projection; bodies with runtime-significant TypeScript tokens are excluded; a candidate is never a fact, never semantic equivalence and never a deletion prerequisite (§6.4).

167	### 1.4 Mixed repositories and workspace units (R1)
168	
169	The v1 rule ("deepest root, then `Cargo.toml` > `tsconfig.json`") was wrong: in a
170	repository whose root holds both `Cargo.toml` and `package.json`/`tsconfig.json`
171	every TypeScript file fell into the Rust unit and silently left the TypeScript
172	program. Units are now **per language family and program membership**, and may
173	share a root.
174	
175	**Reference discovery model** (`discover_units`, `assign_membership` in the model;
176	records `WorkspaceUnitV2`, `FileMembershipRowV1`, `UnitMembershipV1`). The root
177	discovery boundary and trust decision remain the security/foundation owners'
178	(DR-103); this contract defines what happens inside that boundary.
179	
180	`WorkspaceUnitV2` (closed): `{unitOrdinal, rootPath, languageFamily: rust|tsjs|none,
181	languageMode, unitKind: cargo-workspace|cargo-package|ts-program|js-program|syntax-only,
182	markerPath, markerSha256, recognizerId, recognizerVersion, provenance:
183	EXPLICIT|DISCOVERED|DEFAULTED, memberPackageRoots[]}`.
184	
185	- **U-1 (one unit per directory and language family)** A directory holding
186	  `Cargo.toml` yields a `rust` unit; a directory holding `tsconfig.json`,
187	  `jsconfig.json` or `package.json` yields exactly one `tsjs` unit whose mode is
188	  chosen by precedence `tsconfig.json` (→ `ts-tsconfig`/`js-allowjs`) >
189	  `jsconfig.json` (→ `js-allowjs`) > `package.json` (→ `js-synthesized`). The
190	  precedence selects the mode **within** `tsjs`; it never removes the co-located
191	  `rust` unit. A root with both markers has two units with the same `rootPath`
192	  (`units-colocated-cargo-and-package-json-root-keeps-both-languages`).
193	- **U-2 (Cargo workspace folding)** A `Cargo.toml` package inside a Cargo
194	  workspace root's tree is folded into the workspace unit as a member package
195	  (Cargo resolves the workspace as one program); it is listed in
196	  `memberPackageRoots`, not as a separate unit. A standalone package outside any
197	  workspace is its own `cargo-package` unit. **Explicit roots are unit
198	  selection, never loss of Cargo workspace semantics (post-reset v2 A-3/P22):**
199	  naming a Cargo workspace root explicitly yields exactly the automatic result
200	  for that unit (members folded, member `target` output pruned, a member's
201	  `src/target` still source); naming a member package alone selects that package
202	  as its own `cargo-package` unit, and files of the unselected root or siblings
203	  are honest `no-program-unit-for-language` rows, neither claimed nor
204	  over-ignored (`units-explicit-cargo-workspace-root-keeps-member-folding-and-member-target-pruning`).
205	- **U-3 (deterministic membership within a language)** A file's family is fixed
206	  by extension (`.rs` → `rust`; `.ts/.tsx/.mts/.cts/.js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx` → `tsjs`).
207	  It belongs to the **deepest unit of its own family** whose root prefixes its
208	  path. Units of another family never claim it. Nested monorepo packages
209	  (`packages/web/tsconfig.json` under a root `tsconfig.json`) are therefore
210	  distinct `tsjs` units and the deeper one wins for its subtree
211	  (`units-nested-monorepo-deepest-within-language-and-workspace-folding`).
212	- **U-4 (no source erasure; honest unsupported files)** Every snapshot inventory
213	  file appears in exactly one `FileMembershipRowV1`: `program-member`;
214	  `syntax-only` with reason `no-program-unit-for-language` (a `.rs` file with no

216	  `grammar-only` (bundled grammar, no program) or `host-ignore-convention`
217	  (the file lies inside a pruned tree of the shared rule below); or

220	  (`maxItems 0`) and the model refuses a membership that does not cover the

222	- **U-4a (one shared discovery rule; post-reset MUST-3)** The host ignore
223	  conventions and unit enumeration are stated once, in

227	  by **exact path segment** (never substring): dependency trees (`node_modules`),

363	## 2. Semantic universe successors
364	
365	Every array in the current native schema bundle declares `x-opensip-order`
366	under identity §3. `sequence` preserves order and repeated items unless a separate
367	uniqueness constraint applies. It is intentional for compiler flags, signature
368	tokens, substitution precedence and ordered observations. Stricter orders are
369	machine-checked at schema admission: declaration components by `component`,
370	dependency packages by `(name, version, sourceId)`, owner records by `ownerKey`,
371	file-manifest rows by `path`, and the explicitly sorted path/name/enum collections
372	by raw UTF-8 bytes. These keys must be unique; a second row with the same key and
373	different payload also refuses. The canonical encoder never sorts a collection.
374	Input-adapter observation sequences retain their own declared order; a producer
375	must construct any stricter output collection before admitting it.

380	`resolvedInputs` becomes `RustUniverseV2ResolvedInputs`:

382	| Field | Type | Rule |

Every set's `cfg` **contains every member of the context's `baseCfg`**: sets differ from the base only by additions, and `cfgSetId` is unique within the universe. A set that dropped a base cfg would analyse a configuration nothing selected |

Raw file digests are also in the snapshot |

401	**Binding a `rust-v2` universe (`bind_rust_universe`).** A universe is bound to its
402	admitted context before PlanId, exactly as `typescript-v2` is bound by
403	`bind_typescript_universe` (§2.4), and for the same reason: an identity commits to
404	the context bytes, not to the universe's copy of them. The binding is pure — it
405	executes no cargo, rustc, build script, proc macro or filesystem read — and takes
406	the admitted context descriptor, the retained nested input records
407	(`DependencySourceSetV1`, `UnifiedFeaturesV1`, `PreparedOutputSetV3` when one is
408	selected) and the analysed snapshot inventory. All three are **required**: there is
409	no context-free or input-free admit path, because an optional join is not a rule,
410	and omission is the typed refusal `native.universe-retained-inputs-not-supplied`,
411	never an ADMIT. It refuses when

413	- the admission is not a Rust context admission, or the universe names a context
414	  this host did not mint, or the supplied context bytes are not the admitted ones;

416	  `dependencySourceSetId`, `unifiedFeaturesId`, `preparedOutputSetId`, `rustflags`,
417	  `configProjectionSha256`, `executionCapableResolution`, `preparedResolution`, or a
418	  `cfgSets` entry that drops a base cfg or repeats a `cfgSetId`;
419	- a nested semantic identity is not the exact H identity of the retained record of

420	  its registered domain, or that record contradicts the universe or context —

453	`module=node16`, `moduleResolution=node16`, `target=es2022`, `jsx=preserve` iff any
454	`.jsx/.tsx` root exists else absent, `strict=false`, `skipLibCheck=true`,
455	`types=[]`, `noEmit=true`, roots = every `.ts/.tsx/.js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx` file under
456	the unit excluding `node_modules`, `.git` and host ignore conventions. No option is
457	read from the environment. A synthesizer change is a universe change.
