459	### 2.3 `NativeContextV2` (Rust)
460	
461	**There is exactly one native-context record and one `H` domain per language.**
462	`NativeContextV2` is the **Rust** context; `TypeScriptNativeContextV2` (§2.4) is the
463	TypeScript one. Neither is a general "native context": a universe binds the record of its
464	own language and refuses the other.
465	
466	Descriptor (domain `native.context.rust.v2`): `{schemaVersion:2, targetTriple,
467	hostTriple, toolchain: ToolchainIdentityV1, toolClosure: ToolClosureV1, baseCfg,
468	resolverVersion, dependencySourceSetId, unifiedFeaturesId, preparedOutputSetId|null,
469	configProjection: CargoConfigProjectionV2}`.
470	
471	`rustcDevLlvmDigest` is at **`NativeContextV2.toolchain.rustcDevLlvmDigest`**, inside
472	`ToolchainIdentityV1` — not a top-level field of the context (a citation that says only "in
473	native-context schema 2" is reachable but under-specified). Its value is the 64-hex suffix
474	of the `closure2` identity of the admitted `kind=rust-dev-llvm` closure, so `"closure2:" +`
475	the field must name a retained closure of that kind whose recomputed identity equals it;
476	`admit_native_context('rust', …)` performs exactly that join against the retained closure
477	descriptor and tree.
478	
479	`ToolClosureV1` = `{rustc, cargo, linker|null, ar|null, procMacroServer, closureId}`
480	— the raw digests of every executable the adapter may select, all members of the
481	signed `closure2` named by `closureId`. **Every tool that runs is in this
482	closure**: `rustc`, `cargo`, the linker rustc spawns when a build script or
483	proc-macro crate is linked, `ar`, and the proc-macro server. No `PATH` lookup, no
484	system `cc`, no `RUSTC`/`CARGO`/`RUSTUP_*`/`CARGO_HOME` from the environment. If a
485	platform family has no bundled linker in the closure, in-host preparation is
486	`UNSUPPORTED-TYPED` there (`native.execution-not-authorized`, cause
487	`linker-unavailable`); it never falls back to a system linker.
488	
489	The host resolved-inputs adapter computes the context before PlanId; the worker
490	recomputes it after sealed inputs are received and refuses with
491	`Unavailable(native-context-mismatch)` before Analyze if any byte differs (§9.5).
492	
493	### 2.4 `TypeScriptNativeContextV2` (TypeScript/JavaScript)
494	
495	Descriptor (domain `native.context.typescript.v2`): `{schemaVersion:2, languageMode,
496	toolchain: TypeScriptToolchainIdentityV1, toolClosure: TypeScriptToolClosureV1,
497	configProjection: TypeScriptConfigProjectionV2, moduleResolutionMode, packageModuleType,
498	nodeModulesLayoutDigest|null, lockfileIdentity|null}`.
499	
500	`TypeScriptToolchainIdentityV1` = `{compilerName:"typescript", compilerVersion,
501	compilerPackageDigest, typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot, standardLibraryComponentDigests[],
502	libSelection[]}`. `TypeScriptToolClosureV1` = `{compiler, runtime, closureId}`.
503	
504	**Exact field locations and producing recipe.** Every value is computed by the host
505	resolved-inputs adapter before PlanId from **admitted, retained** bytes; none is read from a
506	worker claim, a `tsc --version` string or the environment.
507	
508	| Field | Produced from |
509	|---|---|
510	| `toolchain.compilerVersion` | the `semanticVersion` of the **admitted signed compiler closure manifest** named by `toolClosure.closureId`; admission refuses when the two differ, so a version string and the bytes it labels cannot drift apart |
511	| `toolchain.compilerPackageDigest` | a member digest of that retained `kind=toolchain` closure tree |
512	| `toolchain.typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot` | identity §3's existing recipe: the **64-hex suffix** of the `closure2` identity of the admitted `kind=stdlib` closure. `"closure2:" +` the value must name a retained closure of that kind whose recomputed identity equals it |
513	| `toolchain.standardLibraryComponentDigests` | the **complete** declaration-file inventory of that retained stdlib tree — one row per `.d.ts` member, selected or not, `component` = the member basename, sorted by `component`. A missing row refuses `native.native-context-stdlib-inventory-incomplete:<name>`, because an alternate partial declaration inventory for the same retained library is not the required complete record. A tree in which two paths share a basename refuses `native.native-context-stdlib-tree-ambiguous-basename:<name>` rather than resolving the join arbitrarily |
514	| `toolchain.libSelection` | the effective `lib` names the resolved `compilerOptions` select after `target` defaulting, sorted; each must be covered by a retained component |
515	| `toolClosure.compiler`, `toolClosure.runtime` | raw digests of the bundled compiler and of the bundled JavaScript runtime that executes it, both members of the signed closure named by `closureId`. No `PATH` lookup, no system `node`, no `NODE_OPTIONS`/`NODE_PATH`/`TS_NODE_*` from the environment |
516	| `configProjection.honoredOptions` | the closed subset of the **effective** resolved `compilerOptions` (or of `SynthesizedCompilerOptionsV1` under `js-synthesized`) that changes program membership, module resolution or checking |
517	| `configProjection.strippedOptions` | every option removed, with a typed reason (`selects-an-executable`, `emits-output`, `reads-the-environment`, `acquires-types-from-the-network`, `not-a-resolution-or-membership-option`). Stripping is disclosed here and is never a reason to read the option from anywhere else. `typeAcquisitionEnabled` and `executableSelected` are schema constants `false` |
518	| `configProjection.configGraphPaths` | every `tsconfig`/`jsconfig` file of the resolved `extends` graph, in the snapshot, sorted by logical path; empty under `configOrigin=synthesized` |
519	| `nodeModulesLayoutDigest` | raw SHA-256 of the canonical `resolvedNodeModulesLayout` record, or `null` when `nodeModulesInReadSet=false` |
520	| `lockfileIdentity` | `{kind, path, contentSha256}` of the admitted lockfile, or `null` when `lockfileKind=none` |
521	
522	**Retained trees.** The stdlib closure and the compiler closure are retained **whole** —
523	complete foundation `closure` descriptor and complete file tree — and joined to the selected
524	compiler. `admit_native_context` recomputes each closure identity from its retained record
525	and refuses `native.native-context-closure-unretained`,
526	`native.native-context-closure-identity-mismatch` or
527	`native.native-context-closure-kind-mismatch` before any digest comparison. The stdlib merkle
528	root is therefore never a bare number a caller can assert.
529	
530	**No platform *field*, and the identity is still platform-specific.** Unlike the Rust context there
531	is no `targetTriple`/`hostTriple`, because TypeScript *resolution semantics* — which specifiers
532	resolve, which subjects are examined, what is checked — are platform-invariant by design (§1.1).
533	That is a design selection of this contract, not a measurement, and it is **not** a claim that the
534	identity is platform-invariant: `toolClosure.closureId` names a signed closure whose foundation
535	`closure` descriptor includes `platform`, so the same source analysed with the platform-specific
536	executables of two families mints two `nativeContextId`s — as it must, because different bytes ran
537	(`typescript-context-identity-is-platform-specific-through-its-signed-tool-closure`).
538	
539	**Universe and Plan binding.** `typescript-v2.nativeContextId` is
540	`H("native.context.typescript.v2", descriptor)` in the `Sha256Text` form. `PlanId` binds the
541	same digest through `plan.nativeContextDigests`, which takes the **bare 64 hex** (§11, the
542	foundation `plan` record's spelling) and is a canonical **set**: several units of one language
543	legitimately share one context, and identical admitted contexts collapse to one member — that is
544	deduplication of an identical descriptor, never of two different ones.
545	
546	`bind_typescript_universe(universe, admission, context)` refuses a universe whose `nativeContextId`
547	this host did not mint (`native.universe-context-binding-mismatch`) and refuses a Rust-minted context
548	outright (`native.native-context-language-mismatch`). The **retained context bytes are a required
549	argument**: there is no context-free admit path, because an optional field-agreement check is not a
550	rule — a caller that omitted it would obtain exactly the bypass this join exists to close. Omission
551	is the typed refusal `native.universe-context-not-supplied`
552	(`typescript-universe-bound-without-the-retained-context-refuses`); context bytes that do not hash to
553	the admitted id refuse
554	`native.universe-context-binding-mismatch:context-bytes-are-not-the-admitted-ones`.
555	
556	Given those bytes the two records must **agree where they overlap**: a matching `nativeContextId`
557	commits to the context bytes, not to the universe's copy of them, so `languageMode`,
558	`packageModuleType`, `allowJs`, `checkJs`, `lockfileKind`, `nodeModulesInReadSet`,
559	`jsDiagnosticsEnabled`, `jsAdmittedToProgram`, `configOrigin`, the `extends`-graph emptiness and the
560	synthesized-options presence are each checked against the context and refuse
561	`native.universe-context-field-mismatch:<field>`.
562	
563	The context itself also has mandatory agreement rules. `moduleResolutionMode`
564	equals `configProjection.honoredOptions.moduleResolution`. `libSelection` is
565	strictly sorted by UTF-8 name bytes, contains no case-insensitive duplicate names,
566	and selects the same case-insensitive name set as the honored `lib` list;
567	each record retains its specified order for hashing. The closed resolved context
568	always materializes that nonempty list. When source configuration omits `lib`,
569	the resolver supplies the pinned compiler's target-default library selection
570	in both records; `null` is not an alternate resolved spelling.
571	`standardLibraryComponentDigests`
572	has strictly unique component keys in UTF-8 order. Context admission refuses any
573	contradiction before its digest may enter Plan. In synthesized mode every value
574	in `synthesizedOptions` equals the corresponding honored option, and an absent
575	optional `jsx` means honored `jsx` is null. Presence alone is insufficient.
576	These are semantic agreement checks in addition to closed schema validation;
577	internal diagnostic suffixes remain operational refusal evidence, not new public
578	DomainDetail codes.
579	
580	**Independent derivation (§9.5) applies to TypeScript exactly as to Rust.** The worker
581	recomputes the context from its own sealed inputs; a differing byte is
582	`Unavailable(native-context-mismatch)` before Analyze.

608	## 3. Sealed dependency inputs (AR-07)
609	
610	### 3.1 `DependencySourceSetV1`
611	
612	Identity domain `native.dependency-source-set.v1`. Closed descriptor:
613	`{schemaVersion:1, language:"rust", lockfileIdentity, packages:
614	[DependencyPackageSourceV1…] sorted by (name, version, sourceId) UTF-8 bytes,
615	completeness:{state, missing[]}}`.
616	
617	`DependencyPackageSourceV1`:
618	
619	| Field | Rule |
620	|---|---|
621	| `name`, `version` | exact `[[package]]` values from `Cargo.lock` |
622	| `sourceKind` | `registry \| git \| path \| vendored` |
623	| `sourceId` | exact `source` string from `Cargo.lock`, or `""` for path packages |
624	| `lockChecksum` | 64-hex from the lock `checksum`, or `null` for git/path |
625	| `fileManifestSha256` | H(`native.dependency-file-manifest.v1`, sorted `[{path, contentSha256, byteLength}]`) |
626	| `fileCount`, `totalBytes` | exact uint64 |
627	| `acquisition` | `{mode: in-snapshot-path \| in-snapshot-vendored \| imported-descriptor, descriptorId: ImportId\|null, vendorPath\|null}` |
628	| `checksumVerification` | `tarball-matched \| self-consistent \| not-applicable \| mismatch` — `mismatch` refuses the whole set |
629	| `provenanceAssurance` | `registry-authenticated \| declared` |
630	
631	Verification rules (feedback 3 corrected):
632	
633	- **DS-1 (registry, vendored tree)** A vendored directory carries a self-asserted
634	  `.cargo-checksum.json`. Its `package` field equalling `lockChecksum` proves
635	  nothing about the files: an attacker rewrites file contents and every `files`
636	  entry while preserving `package`. The host therefore checks internal
637	  consistency only (`package == lockChecksum`, every listed file's SHA-256
638	  matches, no extra or missing files) and records `checksumVerification =
639	  self-consistent`, `provenanceAssurance = declared`. Inconsistency is `mismatch`
640	  and refuses the set. The reference model contains the mutation
641	  (`ds1-mutation-preserving-package-checksum-stays-declared`): the mutated tree is
642	  still admitted, and it is still *declared*, never authenticated.
643	- **DS-2 (registry, tarball)** Only the exact `.crate` tarball whose SHA-256
644	  equals `lockChecksum` yields `tarball-matched` / `registry-authenticated`. The
645	  host extracts it deterministically into the CAS and computes the file manifest
646	  itself. An extracted tree plus `.cargo-checksum.json` is DS-1.
647	- **DS-3 (git)** The import supplies the checked-out tree for the exact `#rev`;
648	  `not-applicable` / `declared`; the file manifest identity is the binding.
649	- **DS-4 (path)** Path dependencies live in the snapshot; nothing is imported.
650	- **DS-5 (no ambient reads)** `$CARGO_HOME/registry`, `~/.cargo`, `vendor/`
651	  outside the snapshot, or any host path is read **only** as the explicit,
652	  user-named source path of an import step (§7). Any acquisition mode outside the
653	  closed set, or any fetch URL, refuses. No network fetch exists in any first-party
654	  code path (design invariant, conformance-checked; not a confinement claim).
655	- **DS-6 (completeness)** The set is complete for a target when every package
656	  activated by `UnifiedFeaturesV1` is present with `checksumVerification ≠
657	  mismatch`. An incomplete set is admitted with `completeness.incomplete` and
658	  typed `input-closure-incomplete` Coverage for dependent crates; it never blocks
659	  syntax analysis.
660	
661	`declared` provenance is disclosed wherever the package matters: in the Plan
662	(through the set descriptor), in `AuthorizedExecutionV2.owners[].provenanceAssurance`,
663	and in the pre-execution sentence (§5.2). Facts derived from declared sources are
664	still Plan-bound Coverage inputs; the disclosure is what changes.
665	
666	### 3.2 Custody and transport
667	
668	The host stores admitted dependency sources in its content-addressed store keyed
669	by `fileManifestSha256`; Plan-bound by `dependencySourceSetId`. Transport uses
670	protocol-3 frames `DependencySourceManifest / DependencySourceChunk /
671	DependencySourceSeal / DependencySourceAccepted` (§9.2) with the same byte-exact,
672	digest-verified, reject-before-use discipline as the snapshot. The worker mounts
673	the accepted files read-only at `.opensip/deps/v1/<name>-<version>/…` in its
674	private scratch materialization. Nothing is fetched lazily.
675	
676	### 3.3 Cargo configuration: verified carrier, exact flags (feedback 5, 10)
677	
678	Primary source (`doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html`, read 2026-09-06):
679	Cargo reads `.cargo/config.toml` (and legacy `.cargo/config`) from the current
680	directory and **every ancestor**, plus `$CARGO_HOME/config.toml`, merging arrays;
681	it also honors `CARGO_*` environment overrides and knobs that select executables
682	(`build.rustc`, `build.rustc-wrapper`, `target.*.linker`, `target.*.runner`),
683	credentials and network. Stock Cargo has no switch that disables ancestor
684	discovery, and this contract does not claim `--config` replaces the stack.
685	
686	The first-party `opensip-cargo-adapter` therefore establishes a **verified
687	ancestor carrier** (`CargoConfigProjectionV2`, all checked by
688	`cargo_config_admission` in the model):
689	
690	- **CC-1** Before every Cargo invocation, every ancestor directory of the private
691	  scratch root is checked for `.cargo/config.toml` and `.cargo/config`. Presence
692	  is a refusal (`native.ambient-cargo-config`, exit 4), never a merge and never a
693	  silent skip. `ancestorCarrierVerified=true` is recorded in the context.
694	- **CC-2** `CARGO_HOME` is a fresh private empty directory created for the
695	  invocation; its `config.toml` is absent by construction.
696	- **CC-3** The constructed environment contains no `PATH`, `CARGO_*`, `RUSTFLAGS`,
697	  `RUSTC*`, `RUSTDOC*`, `RUSTUP_*`, `CC`/`CXX`/`LD`/`AR`/`TARGET_*` variables;
698	  presence of any is a refusal. Tool locations are passed as absolute closure
699	  paths on the command line, not via environment.
700	- **CC-4** Every selected tool digest equals its entry in `ToolClosureV1`.
701	- **CC-5** Every `.cargo/config(.toml)` inside the snapshot (any directory, not
702	  only the root) is replaced in the materialization by the single projected file;
703	  the originals remain snapshot bytes for identity but are never read by Cargo.
704	
705	Projected (honored) keys: `build.target`, `build.rustflags`,
706	`target.<triple>.rustflags` (both through the flag allowlist below),
707	`source.<name>.directory` pointing inside the snapshot with `replace-with`,
708	`resolver`, and `[patch]` in `Cargo.toml`. Stripped and recorded: `alias`,
709	`build.rustc`, `build.rustc-wrapper`, `build.rustc-workspace-wrapper`,
710	`build.rustdoc`, `build.target-dir`, `build.build-dir`, `build.incremental`,
711	`build.dep-info-basedir`, `cargo-new`, `credential-alias`, `doc`, `env`,
712	`future-incompat-report`, `http`, `install`, `net`, `patch` (config-level),
713	`profile`, `registries`, `registry`, `target.*.linker`, `target.*.runner`,
714	`target.*.<links>`, `term`, `unstable`. A `[source]` replacement pointing outside
715	the snapshot is `input-closure-incomplete` (`source-replacement-outside-snapshot`).
716	
717	**Two distinct digests, both now named.** `CargoConfigProjectionV2.projectionSha256`
718	is the raw SHA-256 of the exact bytes of the **single projected `.cargo/config.toml`
719	file** the adapter materializes under CC-5 — a raw artifact digest of a file.
720	`rust-v2.configProjectionSha256` (§2.1) is the 64-hex suffix of
721	`H("native.cargo-config-projection.v2", CargoConfigProjectionV2)` over the whole
722	projection record. Neither is the raw SHA-256 of the canonical projection bytes, and
723	neither substitutes for the other. Every `replacedSnapshotConfigs` entry names a
724	path that must be in the analysed snapshot inventory: the originals remain snapshot
725	bytes for identity even though Cargo never reads them.
726	
727	**Rustflags allowlist** (`RustflagsProjectionV1`; primary source
728	`doc.rust-lang.org/rustc/command-line-arguments.html`, read 2026-09-06). Honored,
729	exactly:
730	
731	| Flag | Constraint |
732	|---|---|
733	| `--cfg <ident>` / `--cfg <ident>="<value>"` / `--cfg=<…>` | identifier syntax; no spaces |
734	| `-A/-W/-D/-F <lint>`, `-A<lint>`… and long forms; `--cap-lints <allow\|warn\|deny\|forbid>` | lint name syntax `[a-z0-9_:]+` |
735	| `-C target-feature=…`, `-C target-cpu=…`, `-C opt-level=…`, `-C debuginfo=…`, `-C panic=…`, `-C overflow-checks=…`, `-C debug-assertions=…`, `-C strip=…` | value matches `[A-Za-z0-9_+,.=-]+` |
736	| `--remap-path-prefix <from>=<to>` | only when `<from>` is a verified in-snapshot or in-closure path |
737	
738	Everything else is stripped and disclosed with a typed reason: `@file` response
739	files, `-C linker`, `-C link-arg(s)`, `-C link-self-contained`, `-C codegen-backend`,
740	`-C llvm-args`, `-C extra-filename`, `-L`, `--sysroot`, `--extern`, `-Z…`, `-o`,
741	`--out-dir`, `--emit`, unknown `-C` options, malformed `--cfg`. The projection
742	carries the constant `executableSelected=false`. Stripping a flag is disclosed in
743	the universe; it is never a reason to read the flag from anywhere else.

755	### 3.5 Coverage semantics for missing external crates (`missing-external-crate`)
756	
757	Given crate C depending (directly or transitively via activated edges) on
758	activated external package P absent from the set: `declares/literal/control-flow/
759	clones` for C: `complete`. `imports/references/calls/types` at resolved rungs for
760	C: `unknown`, deficiency `input-closure-incomplete`, cause
761	`missing-dependency-source`, detail `[P]`. Crates not depending on P: unaffected.
762	Remedy text: "vendor or import the sealed source for P"; never "install or enable

765	### 3.6 `PreparedOutputSetV3`: inert rows only (feedback 4, R2)
766	
767	Domain `native.prepared-output-set.v3` (revised in place; v3 was never accepted).
768	`{schemaVersion:3, preparation: {kind: authorized-execution|imported-descriptor,
769	authorizationId|null, importId|null, toolchain, dependencySourceSetId, cfgSetId,
770	producer}, rows: [PreparedOutputRowV3…]}`.
771	
772	`PreparedOutputRowV3`: `{kind, ownerKey, configuration, site|null, generated|null,
773	inputBinding: {ownerFileManifestSha256, dependencySourceSetId, toolchainDigest,
774	cfgSetId}, blob: {sha256, byteLength, mediaType}, status: ok|failed,
775	failureDetail|null}`.
776	
777	- **PO-0 (inert by kind and consumption channel; a media type is a label, never a
778	  trust proof)** Admissible row kinds are exactly three:
779	  `build-script-directives` (`text/x-cargo-directives`: the captured `cargo:`
780	  lines, including `rustc-cfg`/`rustc-env` consumed by `cfg`/`env!`),
781	  `macro-expansion` (`text/x-rust-expansion`: the fully expanded token text for one
782	  invocation `site` = `{path, startByte, endByte, inputTokenDigest}`), and
783	  `generated-file` (`generated = {logicalPath, blob}` with media type
784	  `text/x-rust-source`, `text/plain` or `application/octet-stream`: one data file
785	  a build script wrote under `OUT_DIR`). Row kinds `proc-macro-dylib` and
786	  `build-script-binary` are refused **regardless of the media type they claim**
787	  (a dylib relabelled `text/x-rust-expansion` is still a dylib row), and a media
788	  type outside the kind's set is refused; either is
789	  `native.prepared-output-not-inert` (exit 2), from an import *and* from the
790	  in-host step alike (`generated-file-media-type-is-not-trust-proof-kind-decides`).
791	  **No prepared artifact is ever loaded, linked or executed by the semantic
792	  worker.** Expansions are looked up by exact
793	  `(path, span, inputTokenDigest, macro crate manifest)`; a miss is a
794	  `macro-expansion-unavailable` edge (L-RS4).
795	- **PO-4 (generated-file input closure and the read-only virtual `OUT_DIR`)**
796	  The worker resolves `env!("OUT_DIR")` for owner *O* to the read-only virtual
797	  path `.opensip/out/v1/<ownerKey>/` in its sealed VFS. A site
798	  `include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/generated.rs"))` (likewise
799	  `include_str!`/`include_bytes!`) reads the `generated-file` row bound to
800	  `(ownerKey, logicalPath="generated.rs")` whose `inputBinding` equals the current
801	  context, and consumes its bytes **only** as Rust source text, a string literal or
802	  a byte literal respectively. A miss (no row, stale binding, failed owner) is a
803	  typed unknown: `build-script-generated-unavailable` edge, cause
804	  `generated-file-missing`; it is never a hard failure and never a fallback to a
805	  host path (`generated-file-include-out-dir-resolves-inert`,
806	  `generated-file-missing-is-typed-unknown-not-failure`). Strict bounds
807	  (`GeneratedInputBoundsV1`): `logicalPath` is a strict relative path (no `/`
808	  prefix, no `.`/`..` segment, no NUL or backslash, ≤ 1024 bytes; an escaping path
809	  fails exact typed admission and the worker lookup independently refuses it with
810	  cause `generated-file-out-of-bounds`), `maxGeneratedFilesPerOwner 4096`,
811	  `maxGeneratedFileBytes 67108864`, `maxGeneratedTotalBytes 1073741824`,
812	  `maxGeneratedFileRows 1000000` (protocol limit). Imported blobs are bound to
813	  archive members by exact `blobs[]` digest; an archive member outside the
814	  wrapper's `blobs` is never read (`generated-file-path-escape-and-bounds-refused`).
815	- **PO-1 (staleness)** A row is usable only if `inputBinding` equals the current
816	  context (owner manifest, dependency set, toolchain digest, cfg set). A stale row
817	  is refused before Plan construction (`REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`, detail
818	  `native.stale-prepared-output`, listing the differing fields) when prepared mode
819	  was selected explicitly, or is ignored with a disclosed `staleRows` list and
820	  non-prepared fallback when prepared mode was defaulted. It never uses a stale blob.
821	- **PO-2 (failed rows)** A `failed` build script is retained as a row so the same
822	  inputs need not be re-run; the owner is analyzed non-prepared
823	  (`build-script-generated-unavailable`).
824	- **PO-3 (imported)** An imported set carries the same binding fields and
825	  `provenanceAssurance: declared`; the host cannot verify that an external
826	  preparer produced the expansions faithfully. Facts derived from them are
827	  Plan-bound and disclosed with the import identity and producer.
828	
829	Where do the expansions and generated files come from? From the **preparation
830	step** (§5.3), which is the only place proc-macro dylibs are built and loaded and
831	build scripts run, inside the authorized `repository-code` principal with live
832	boundaries. The step captures the required generated **data** and discards every
833	executable product; its output is the inert row set, and the worker consumes only
834	that.

838	## 4. Resolution completeness (AR-12)
839	
840	### 4.1 Two different completeness claims
841	
842	A Coverage entry commits two things that were previously conflated:
843	
844	1. **Examined universe** — the exhaustive examined subject/target partition
845	   (`subjectScopeCommitment`, retained). "Did we look at every subject?"
846	2. **Resolution completeness** — whether every reference/import/call edge
847	   originating in the examined subjects was resolved to a binding at the requested
848	   rung, *after resolution was actually attempted over the whole partition*.
849	   "Could we see every consumer?"
850	
851	### 4.1a Producing recipe for `subjectScopeCommitment` (closed)
852	
853	The retained C-2 selector deferred computation and verification. This is the successor
854	recipe; nothing about the historical artifact changes.
855	
856	**Recipe.** `subjectScopeCommitment` is the foundation **subject-scope** identity of the
857	examined partition, re-spelled in the native `Sha256Text` text form:
858	
859	```
860	scope2      = identity-and-evidence H("subject-scope", D)          -> "scope2:"  + hex
861	commitment  = "sha256:" + the same 64 hex                          -> Sha256Text
862	```
863	
864	where `D` is the closed foundation record
865	`identity-schemas.v2.json#/$defs/subject-scope`
866	`{schemaVersion: 2, snapshotId, sourceUniverse, targetUniverse, relation, resolution,
867	enumeratorClosure, subjects}`.
868	
869	**Inputs, exactly, and where each comes from.** `snapshotId` is the admitted `snapshot2`.

870	`relation`/`resolution` are the Coverage key's own relation and rung. `sourceUniverse` and
871	`targetUniverse` are the bare 64-hex universe digests of the same key (§2, §11).
872	`enumeratorClosure` is the `closure2` of the Plan-bound enumerator that produced the
873	partition. `subjects` is the **complete** examined subject inventory that enumerator
874	enumerated over that snapshot, a canonical set (foundation ordering, duplicates refuse
875	rather than dedupe). **Encoding**: the foundation canonical encoder and `H` frame, imported,
876	not restated. There is **no native `H` domain for this field**: one preimage, one digest,
877	two admitted textual spellings (§11).
878	
879	**Join with `scope2`.** The commitment is the *identical* digest to the `scope2` the host
880	binds into the `coverage2` descriptor (`coverage.scopeId`). It is therefore not a second
881	commitment and cannot drift from the scope it names. Its purpose is that the Coverage
882	*payload* — the bytes whose `payloadDigest` mints `coverage2` — carries the provider's
883	in-band commitment to the partition it claims to have examined, which the host then checks
884	against a value the provider never supplied.
885	
886	**Where it is produced and checked (`admit_coverage_result_v3`, the admitted native producer
887	boundary).** For every `CoverageResultV3` a provider sends, before any `coverage2` exists:
888	
889	1. The host builds `D` from **its own** enumeration and mints `scope2`. A provider-supplied
890	   commitment is never an input to this step.
891	2. `key.relation`, `key.resolution`, `key.sourceUniverse`, `key.targetUniverse` must equal
892	   `D`'s (`native.coverage-key-scope-mismatch:<field>`).
893	3. `key.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the computed commitment
894	   (`native.subject-scope-commitment-mismatch`).
895	4. `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the key's
896	   (`native.examined-universe-commitment-mismatch`) and
897	   `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectCount` must equal `len(D.subjects)`
898	   (`native.examined-universe-subject-count-mismatch`). A provider that examined a narrower
899	   partition than the host enumerated is detected here, and by nothing else.
900	5. RC-2 (§4.3) is rechecked over the same partition.
901	6. Only then is `coverage2` minted from `{schemaVersion: 2, scopeId, payloadSchemaDigest,
902	   payloadDigest}`. `payloadSchemaDigest` is the raw SHA-256 of the **exact registered schema
903	   DOCUMENT bytes** (§7.2). A caller may restate it but never choose it: a value that is not the
904	   registered document's digest refuses `native.coverage-payload-schema-not-registered`
905	   (`coverage-payload-schema-digest-a-caller-chose-is-refused`).
906	
907	Every refusal above is `PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION` (`operational-failed` 4) under the §10
908	fault law: a worker that lies about its partition contributes no facts, no Coverage and no
909	Run. This is not a Coverage deficiency; an admitted-but-incomplete input is (§10).
910	
911	**Coverage use (`coverage_view_use`).** A `view2` may name a `coverage2` only if that
912	`coverage2` was admitted at the boundary above and its `scope2` is one of the view's own
913	`scopeIds`. A hash-valid `coverage2` whose subject scope sits outside the evaluated view is
914	refused exactly as hidden finding evidence is (identity §3), rather than joined silently.
915	
916	**No circularity.** `D` names the snapshot, the universes and the enumerator closure. A
917	universe descriptor (§2) names its native context, tools and config projection; a native
918	context names closures; none of them names a scope, a Coverage, a view, an evidence record
919	or a Run. The derivation order is therefore total and acyclic: closures → native context →
920	universe → `scope2` → commitment → Coverage payload → `coverage2` → `view2`. The foundation
921	scope *descriptor* whose raw digest is `scopeDigest` (§1.4, workspace roots and path
922	prefixes) is a different record with a different job and is not this commitment.
923	
924	Cases: `subject-scope-commitment-is-the-scope2-identity-in-native-sha256-text-form`,
925	`subject-scope-commitment-binds-the-snapshot-not-only-the-subject-list`,
926	`coverage-admission-mints-coverage2-from-the-host-subject-scope`,
927	`coverage-commitment-chosen-by-the-claimant-is-refused`,
928	`coverage-producer-chosen-narrower-examined-partition-is-refused`,
929	`coverage-examined-subject-count-that-disagrees-with-the-enumeration-is-refused`,
930	`coverage-key-naming-a-universe-outside-the-host-scope-is-refused`,
931	`coverage-complete-claimed-over-an-admitted-unresolved-edge-is-refused-at-the-boundary`,
932	`coverage-incomplete-over-an-exhaustive-partition-admits-with-the-same-commitment`,
933	`coverage-use-requires-the-subject-scope-to-be-in-the-evaluated-view`,
934	`coverage2-whose-subject-scope-is-outside-the-view-is-refused`,
935	`coverage2-never-admitted-at-the-producer-boundary-is-refused-in-a-view`,
936	`subject-scope-duplicate-subject-refuses-rather-than-silently-deduping`,
937	`coverage-payload-schema-digest-a-caller-chose-is-refused`. The two positive coverage cases
938	recompute the expected `coverage2` with `hashlib` from the scope, the registered schema-document
939	digest and the canonical payload rather than pinning a literal, so a schema-document edit moves the
940	identity visibly instead of silently invalidating a frozen value.
941	
942	**Coordination (identity owner).** Identity §3 now states the same recipe in its own words —
943	`subjectScopeCommitment` is `"sha256:"` plus the 64-hex suffix of the admitted `scope2` identity,
944	"another textual form of the **same** digest, not a separate hash of the subjects or of the scope
945	identifier string" — and names the same descriptor fields and the same `subjectCount` rule. The two
946	statements agree; this section is the native-side normative detail (the producer boundary, the
947	refusal vocabulary and the coverage-use join) and adds no second recipe. Any future divergence
948	between them is a defect in whichever document moved.

950	Claim 1 never implies claim 2. The counterexample: module A exports `foo`; module
951	B does `import * as m from './a'` then `m[k]()` with `k` a runtime string. Every
952	subject is examined, `m` resolves, `m[k]` has no admissible fact at any rung of
953	`references`, so the v1 view reads `coverage=complete` and a "no consumer of `foo`"

956	`resolutionCompleteness.state=incomplete`; the predicate reports
957	`resolution-incomplete` and `foo`/`bar` are both marked affected (§4.5). Both
958	behaviors are executable in the reference model (`computed-access-m-k`, v1 oracle

1083	
1084	Evaluated in this order; every applicable cause is collected and the most specific
1085	by §10 precedence is reported. `satisfied=true` may carry `disclosures`.
1086	
1087	1. Relation absent from the view → `required-relation-missing`.
1088	2. Rung below `minResolution` → the rung-unavailable cause (`language-tier-unsupported`, `provider-unavailable`, `input-closure-incomplete`, `budget-exhausted`) else `required-relation-missing`.

1136	### 5.1 Principal class `repository-code` and its joins (R4)
1137	
1138	The security contract S10 registers principal class `repository-code`
1139	(`RepoExecutionGrantV2`, execution classes `build-script | proc-macro |
1140	test-runner`). One principal, three current spellings, joined explicitly and
1141	checked by schema constants:
1142	
1143	| Where | Spelling | Role |
1144	|---|---|---|
1145	| security S10 / `AuthorizedExecutionV2.principalClass` | `repository-code` | principal class of the admitted grant |
1146	| foundation `identity-schemas.v2#semantic-grant.principals[].kind` / `AuthorizedExecutionV2.semanticGrantPrincipalKind` | `trusted-repository-code` | Plan-bound semantic projection `{kind, closureId (tool closure), ownerSourceDigest (owner file manifest)}` with `analysisOperations ∋ prepare-code` |

1149	The **authority grant** is the operational `authorizationRef`
1150	(`H("security.repo-execution-grant.v2", grant)`, the workflow's `securityGrantRef`):
1151	it is excluded from the Plan descriptor and from every content identity
1152	(`authorized-execution-interactive-with-declared-owner-disclosed` checks
1153	`authorizationRefInPlan=false`). The **semantic grant projection** is what the Plan
1154	binds. A universe with `preparedResolution=imported-inert` projects only
1155	`read-import`; only `host-prepared` projects `prepare-code`. Prepared semantic
1156	availability therefore never implies that this host holds or held an execution
1157	grant (`prepared-imported-inert-implies-no-host-execution-grant`).

1159	The principal, identified by `{projectId, snapshotId, ownerKey,
1160	ownerFileManifestSha256, toolchainDigest}`, is **outside** the first-party TCB.
1161	Executing it in-host is a disclosed trusted-code execution of code the user chose
1162	to analyze; OpenSIP does not vouch for it and does not confine it unless a
1163	platform primitive is enforced. The security owner supplies the revocation clock
1164	and cancellation carrier (H-2).

1184	JSON output: "Build scripts and procedural macros from N packages will run with
1185	your user's authority. OpenSIP does not prevent network access or other effects on
1186	this platform." followed, when applicable, by "Packages with declared
1187	(unauthenticated) provenance: …".

1189	Authorization: interactive → explicit per-invocation confirmation naming the
1190	owners; CI (`ci=true`) → never prompts; requires a pre-existing `policy-record`
1191	bound to the same `dependencySourceSetId` and toolchain, else
1192	`REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` / `native.execution-not-authorized`. Missing live
1193	boundaries, an unavailable bundled linker, or an over-claimed enforcement value

1195	snapshot with a different owner manifest, or toolchain.

1197	### 5.3 What the preparation step does (feedback 4)
1198	
1199	Owned by the host resolved-inputs adapter (never the semantic worker), after
1200	snapshot seal and dependency-source admission, before PlanId:
1201	
1202	1. Verify the carrier (§3.3 CC-1..CC-5); materialize snapshot and dependency
1203	   sources read-only in private scratch; write the single projected
1204	   `.cargo/config.toml`; construct the environment.
1205	2. Check current trust and revocation state (security owner's clock), then for
1206	   each owner in order: re-check revocation (`before-each-owner`), run the bundled
1207	   Cargo to compile and execute the build script or to build the proc-macro crate
1208	   for the selected cfg set (`cargo check --offline --frozen --locked --target
1209	   <triple>` restricted to the owners; the linker used is the closure linker;
1210	   nothing is installed).
1211	3. **Inside this same authorized step**, drive the bundled compiler's expansion
1212	   through the closure proc-macro server for every invocation site in the
1213	   workspace and dependency crates that names one of the built proc-macro crates,
1214	   and capture the expanded token text per site as `macro-expansion` rows; capture
1215	   `cargo:` directive output as `build-script-directives` rows. Loading the
1216	   proc-macro dylib *is* executing repository code; it happens here, under the
1217	   principal, with the live boundaries, and nowhere else.
1218	4. **Capture required generated data, discard executable products** (R2). For
1219	   each build-script owner: capture the `cargo:` directive lines as a
1220	   `build-script-directives` row; capture as `generated-file` rows the regular
1221	   data files under `OUT_DIR` named by the crate's
1222	   `include!/include_str!/include_bytes!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), …))` sites when
1223	   those are statically determinable, else every regular data file under
1224	   `OUT_DIR` within the PO-4 bounds; discard the build-script binary, every
1225	   dylib/object/archive/executable product and unreferenced scratch files; discard
1226	   the proc-macro dylibs. Referenced paths the script did not produce are recorded
1227	   (`missingReferencedPaths`) and become typed unknowns at analysis. Nothing of
1228	   `OUT_DIR` survives except the captured data rows
1229	   (`preparation-capture-keeps-referenced-data-discards-executable-products`).
1230	   The result is `PreparedOutputSetV3` (`kind: authorized-execution`).
1231	
1232	The semantic worker then consumes the inert set through the protocol
1233	(`PreparedOutputManifest/Chunk/Seal`), looks up expansions by exact site key, and
1234	executes nothing. `RepositoryResolutionV3.workerExecutesRepositoryCode` is the
1235	constant `false`. An external preparer may supply the same inert shape
1236	(`kind: imported-descriptor`, `declared` provenance, §3.6 PO-3); it can never
1237	supply a dylib.

1239	### 5.4 Failure, retry, cancellation, recovery
1240	
1241	| Event | Outcome |
1242	|---|---|
1243	| Owner build script exits non-zero | row `failed`; other owners continue; owner analyzed non-prepared |
1244	| Revocation observed before an owner | step stops; no further owner runs; rows already captured are discarded; `request-rejected` (`native.execution-not-authorized`) |
1245	| Wall or byte bound exceeded | whole step `operational-failed` (4); no row admitted. Existing `HOST.IO_FAILURE` with detail `native.prepare-bound-exceeded`. Not `BudgetExhausted`: a preparation bound is a safety bound of the adapter |
1246	| Cancellation | kill the process group, discard partial OUT_DIR and captured rows, `interrupted` (130) |
1247	| Retry | idempotent by `(dependencySourceSetId, toolchainDigest, cfgSetId, owners manifest)`; an identical inert set already in custody is reused without re-execution and without re-prompt when a policy record covers it |
1248	| Host crash mid-step | scratch reclaimed by ordinary crash reconciliation; no partial set is visible to Plan construction |
1249	| Ambient Cargo config found | `operational-failed` (4), `native.ambient-cargo-config`; never merged |
1250	| Imported set replaces in-host preparation | allowed; PO-0/PO-1/PO-3 apply |

1262	## 6. Clone equivalence modes (AR-13)
1263	
1264	### 6.1 Modes and evidence levels
1265	
1266	| Mode | Level/algorithm | Evidence level (closed) | Authority |
1267	|---|---|---|---|
1268	| `exact` | `L0-verbatim` | `byte-identical` | fact |
1269	| `normalized` | `L1-lexical` (default) or `L2-comment-insensitive` (opt-in) | `lexically-identical` / `comment-insensitive-identical` | fact |
1270	| `structural` | `L3-identifier-insensitive` | `identifier-insensitive-identical` | fact |
1271	| `near` | `near-v1`: Jaccard over 5-gram shingles of the L3 token stream | `similar-candidate` | candidate only |
1272	| `cross-tsjs` | `tsjs-erasure-v1` projection, then L3 | `cross-language-syntax-candidate` / `excluded` | candidate only |
1273	
1274	No semantic equivalence is inferred by any mode.
1275	
1276	### 6.2 Parameters (selected)
1277	
1278	`minOccurrences 2`; `minBodyBytes 64` (exact); `minTokens 20` (L1–L3,
1279	cross-tsjs); `minTokens 50` (near); `nearThreshold 800000` millionths;
1280	`maxCandidatesPerGroup 4096`; `maxGroupsPerUniverse 1000000`.
1281	
1282	### 6.3 Bodies and language-specific exclusions
1283	
1284	Body spans are function, method, closure/lambda, `impl` item and block bodies.
1285	**Import exclusion means candidate exclusion, not byte editing** (R5): a span that
1286	consists solely of import/`use`/`extern crate`/top-level `require` declarations,
1287	module/file headers, shebangs, license headers, `#![...]` inner attributes or
1288	`declare`-only TypeScript declarations is an *import-only body* and is excluded
1289	as a clone candidate in every mode. A body that is kept is hashed over its
1290	**exact verbatim bytes**: an internal `use`, `import()`, `require` or directive
1291	inside a function body is part of the preimage and is never stripped, rewritten
1292	or normalized away at L0 (`clone-import-only-body-excluded-and-kept-bodies-hash-verbatim`:
1293	two bodies differing only by an internal `use` line are not exact clones).
1294	
1295	| Language | Kept significant at every level | L2 removes | L3 renames |
1296	|---|---|---|---|
1297	| TypeScript/JavaScript | string/template literal contents, regex literals, JSX text, `'use strict'`/`'use client'` directives, `/// <reference>` and `// @ts-*` directives, decorators | non-directive comments | local `let/const/var`, parameters, local function names, destructured locals; **not** properties, imports, exports, globals, `this` members |
1298	| Rust | macro invocation token trees verbatim, attributes including `#[cfg]`, string/byte/raw literals, lifetimes | non-doc comments | local `let` bindings, parameters, closure parameters, pattern bindings; **not** fields, paths, generics, trait names, macro-introduced names |
1299

1300	Fact identity is same-language: `languageId ∈ {typescript, javascript, rust}` is
1301	in the preimage, so a TypeScript body never groups with a JavaScript or Rust body
1302	in `exact`/`normalized`/`structural`, even with identical bytes.
1303	
1304	### 6.4 TS/JS cross-language decision (feedback 9)
1305	
1306	Decision: `languageId` **stays** in exact fact identities (a `.ts` and a `.js`
1307	body are different facts). Cross-TS/JS matching is a separate **candidate-only**
1308	mode `cross-tsjs` under the named deterministic syntax projection
1309	`tsjs-erasure-v1`:
1310	
1311	- Removed before L3 normalization: type annotations, `type`/`interface`
1312	  declarations, type parameter lists, `as` assertions, `satisfies`, non-null `!`,
1313	  definite-assignment `!`, `declare`/`readonly`/`abstract`/access modifiers,
1314	  `implements` clauses, `import type`/`export type`.
1315	- **Never removed**: tokens that TypeScript compiles into runtime behavior —
1316	  `enum`/`const enum`, parameter properties (`constructor(private x)`),
1317	  value-bearing `namespace`, decorators, `import =`. A body containing any of them
1318	  is **excluded** from cross matching with reason
1319	  `runtime-significant-ts-tokens` and the token list; it is not projected.
1320	- Output rows carry `projectionId=tsjs-erasure-v1`, `authority=candidate-only`,
1321	  `semanticEquivalenceClaimed=false`, `automaticDeletionEligible=false` as schema
1322	  constants. A cross candidate is never a baseline member, never a Control input,
1323	  never a repair prerequisite.
1324	
1325	Cases: `clone-cross-tsjs-candidate-only`, `clone-cross-tsjs-runtime-significant-excluded`.

1327	### 6.5 Reviewed suppressions and false-positive boundary
1328	
1329	`CloneSuppressionV1` is a superseded draft transport shape, admitted by no product
1330	command. The single current review/suppression record is workflow ReviewDisposition.
1331	Its stable candidate key, mandatory finite expiry and advisory-only semantics are

1333	expired suppressions resurface. Fixed by

1336	comments → L1 not clones, L2 clones; identical bytes in two languages → never a

1476	### 9.1 Versions and identity negotiation (feedback 1)
1477	
1478	`rust-semantic` protocol major **3**; `typescript-semantic` protocol major **2**.
1479	Capability tokens (closed, `CapabilityToken`): identity tokens
1480	`source-identity-snapshot2`, `plan-identity-plan2`, `fact-identity-fact2`,
1481	`coverage-v3`; plus `sealed-vfs-v1`, `multi-stage-analyze-v1`,
1482	`<lang>-semantic-facts-v1`, `resolution-completeness-v2`, `unresolved-edge-v1`,

1489	1. **Plan time (no spawn).** The host reads the signed capability row. The four
1490	   identity tokens are required for every worker; a row lacking any of them, or

1496	   array and identity versions; mismatch → `FAULT`, `PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION`,

1499	   including `nativeContext`, and `RepositoryResolutionV3`. The host state
1500	   machine admits it only when `identityNegotiated=true`; otherwise the run faults
1501	   with `sourceBytesSent=false` (`protocol3-open-universe-without-identity-faults`).
1502	4. Snapshot custody, dependency-source custody, prepared custody,
1503	   `NativeContextVerified`, then Analyze.

61	## 1. Invocation, step, attempt, Run (AR-08)
62	
63	An invocation is one host request. Its operational identity is `RequestId`, minted
64	before admission and retained for refusal as well as success. The invocation is an
65	ordered acyclic list of at most **64 steps**; `StepId` is the zero-based position.
66	Each admitted attempt of a step receives a fresh `ExecutionId`; a step has at most
67	**3 attempts**. Only `analysis` and `verify` steps seal or link a content-derived
68	`run2`. `comparison`, `query`, `render`, `import`, `repair-preview`, `repair-apply`,
69	`test-execution`, `native-preparation`, `mutation`, `export-delivery` and `doctor` are operational steps
70	that never mint a Run. Schema: `invocation-record.schema.json`.
71	
72	**Step DAG versus derivation DAG.** The step list is the operational workflow. Each
73	analysis/verify *attempt* owns exactly one derivation DAG (`exec-plan2`, at most
74	**1024 stages**) recorded in the attempt's `derivation` binding
75	(`planId`, `executionPlanId`, `stageCount`, `stagesCompleted`, `firstFailedStage`).
76	A step never depends on a stage and a stage never references a step. A retry on
77	identical admitted inputs may bind the same `exec-plan2` and the same Run; attempts
78	remain separately auditable.
79	
80	**Dependencies.** `dependsOn` names lower StepIds only (a forward or self reference is
81	`WORKFLOW.DEPENDENCY_CYCLE`, request-rejected). `requirement` is `required` or
82	`optional`; a required step may not depend on an optional step
83	(`WORKFLOW.REQUIRED_DEPENDS_ON_OPTIONAL`). `dependencyGate` is `completed` (every
84	dependency completed) or `terminal` (every dependency reached any terminal outcome;
85	lawful only for `render`/`export-delivery`, which project whatever happened). A
86	step whose gate is unmet is `skipped` with a typed `skipReason`. Step outcomes are
87	closed: `completed`, `rejected`, `failed`, `skipped`, `cancelled`, `abandoned`
88	(crash recovery only).
89	
90	**Retries.** `retryPolicy=idempotent-retry` is lawful only for `analysis`, `verify`,
91	`query`, `render`, `doctor` and `export-delivery`, only for `faultCause=ledger-busy`,
92	and within the 3-attempt budget; exhausting it is `LEDGER.BUSY_TIMEOUT` (4) with
93	detail `WORKFLOW.RETRY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`. `host-io` and every other fault are never
94	retried. `mutation`, `import`, `repair-preview`, `repair-apply`, `comparison`, `native-preparation` and `test-execution`
95	carry `retryPolicy=none` by schema; a spec violating this is refused.
96	
97	**Mutation idempotence and recovery.** Repair apply uses the raw SHA-256 of
98	canonical `{operation:"repair-apply",projectId,repairPlanId,baseSnapshotId}` as its
99	idempotency key. An equal completed key performs no second effect. The original
100	receipt is immutable; a replay delivery produces a separately identified receipt
101	with the new request/attempt binding and `replayed=true`. Mutation receipts use
102	`receipt2:` plus `H('workflow.mutation-receipt', receiptWithoutReceiptId)` and remain
103	retained when an effect or later verification fails. Read-only recovery inspection
104	is distinct from separately authorized recovery writes (§6).
105	
106	**Audit gate ownership.** An analysis step declares `verdictGate=self|delegated`.
107	`self` applies its Run verdict. `delegated` requires authoritative analysis and a
108	consuming comparison step: a completed failing Run then contributes operational
109	success with its RunId, while the comparison owns the regression gate. This lets
110	inherited findings remain visible without failing the PR. Missing required Coverage
111	still contributes indeterminate; delegation cannot hide an incomplete analysis.
112	The comparison result is a distinct closed `ComparisonStepResult`, never a Run.
113	
114	**Cancellation.** A signal is recorded with the phase at which it arrived.
115	*before-settle* (some required step not yet terminal): remaining steps are
116	`cancelled`, the aggregate is `interrupted` (130), and a Run committed by an earlier
117	step is named in the termination's `runId`. *after-settle* (every required step
118	already terminal): the aggregate is **not reclassified**; the settled class stands.
119	Per kind: an analysis attempt aborts and leaves no Run; an import discards its
120	staged bytes; a repair-apply honours cancellation only before `APPLYING`, and during
121	the bounded rename loop the journal, not the signal, decides (§6).
122	
123	**Aggregate termination (D9 ordering preserved).** Over required steps only:
124	`operational-failed` > `request-rejected` > `policy-failed` > `indeterminate` >
125	`success`. An optional step's rejection or failure never changes the aggregate.
126	Policy fail dominates indeterminate across steps exactly as inside one Run, and a
127	required operational fault dominates a committed failing Run (its `runId` is still
128	carried). Exit code derives from class by the fixed table only. Ties retain the first
129	termination carrying domain detail in step order, or the first termination when
130	none carries detail, so a useful comparison remedy is preserved.
131	
132	**Ephemeral analysis.** `--ephemeral` produces the second member of the closed
133	`AnalysisResult` union: `authority=ephemeral`, `durability=not-required`, no `runId`,
134	no receipt, only semantic `planId`/`evidenceId` so the result can be cited. It cannot
135	satisfy baseline adoption, repair preview/apply, verify or authoritative replay
136	(`WORKFLOW.EPHEMERAL_CANNOT_SUPPLY_AUTHORITY`, `REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE`, exit 2). A
137	failing ephemeral verdict terminates `policy-failed` with `authority=ephemeral`
138	instead of a `runId`; the branch contract admits exactly one of the two.
139	
140	**Default invocation.** `opensip` with no arguments is discovery then one durable
141	authoritative analysis (steps `analysis`, `render`). Retention is DEFAULTED
142	durable-unbounded (CD-RT-5), disclosed with the storage root before first write.
143	No policy file is written implicitly.

147	## 2. Portable baseline and runnable prior detector (AR-10)
148	
149	`BaselineArtifactV1` lives in the repository as tracked intent
150	(`opensip.baseline.json`). `baselineId = H('workflow.baseline', descriptor)`. The
151	descriptor pins: origin ProjectId, source `snapshot2`, the **authoritative** `run2`
152	and `plan2` (an ephemeral result is refused: `BASELINE.SOURCE_EPHEMERAL`), the
153	fingerprint recipe (`finding-fingerprint`, major ≥ 2), every contributing detector's
154	`closure2` with semantics major, the complete **pivot closure** (detector executable,
155	evaluator, toolchain/stdlib, schema set; each a `closure2` with manifest digest,
156	protocol major and platform), the evaluation context digests, the **embedded**
157	policy/scope/waiver documents whose digests equal those context digests, rule
158	coverage, and sorted unique entries. Custody (outside identity) carries host release,
159	export time, `retentionPins` (the Run and every pivot closure) and an optional signed
160	`closureBundle` reference.
161	
162	**Fresh CI.** Comparison never reads the origin machine's store. A fresh host admits
163	the artifact by recomputing `baselineId`, checking schema major, recipe major,
164	sortedness, context-document digests and project correspondence (same ProjectId, or
165	explicit `--accept-origin`, else `BASELINE.PROJECT_UNMAPPED` and no comparison). It
166	resolves each pivot closure from (a) a retained generation, (b) an installed signed
167	release with the same `closure2`, or (c) the signed closure bundle; all under
168	**current trust**. A closure that is missing (`pivot-detector-unavailable`), revoked
169	(`pivot-closure-revoked`) or incompatible with the host's protocol majors/platform
170	(`pivot-closure-incompatible`) makes E0 unavailable; a revoked closure is never
171	executed, whatever bytes are present.
172	
173	**Detector semantics.** Semantics can change within a major, so two-way comparison
174	is lawful only when the closures are identical (`identical-closure`) or the current
175	detector's signed manifest lists the baseline `closure2` as exactly semantically
176	compatible at the same major (`declared-compatible`). Otherwise the baseline detector
177	must run over current source (`three-way-pivot`, an authoritative pivot analysis step
178	planned before the primary one) or the detector's entries are `INDETERMINATE`.
179	Fingerprint dual emission (`legacyFingerprint`) migrates identity only and never
180	supplies the prior algorithm. Adoption pins the Run and the pivot closures as
181	retention roots; loss of a pin is disclosed as partial availability and yields typed
182	indeterminacy, never a silent two-way fallback. `baseline-upgrade` re-adopts under the
183	current detector explicitly and is a mutation with its own receipt.

187	## 3. Multi-axis comparison (AR-11)
188	
189	`ComparisonResultV1` (`comparison2:` = `H('workflow.comparison', descriptor)`)
190	attributes every fingerprint to the **first** axis at which it changes along a fixed
191	counterfactual chain evaluated over *current* source:
192	
193	| Pivot | Facts from | Policy | Scope | Waivers |
194	|---|---|---|---|---|
195	| B | baseline artifact entries | prior | prior | prior |
196	| E0 | prior detector closure over current source | prior | prior | prior |
197	| E1 | current detector | prior | prior | prior |
198	| E2 | current detector | current | prior | prior |
199	| E3 | current detector | current | current | prior |
200	| E4 | current Run | current | current | current |
201	
202	Axis order is code (B→E0), detection (E0→E1), policy (E1→E2), scope (E2→E3),
203	waiver (E3→E4, by waived status). E1–E3 are pure re-evaluations of retained current
204	facts under the baseline's embedded documents. They are available only when their
205	results were actually bound; an unchanged axis is `not-needed`, and a required
206	unbound re-evaluation is `unavailable` with typed indeterminacy. E0 is
207	`not-needed` when the detector is unchanged or declared compatible, `available`
208	when the pivot ran, `unavailable` otherwise. Classifications are `UNCHANGED`,
209	`CODE-NET-NEW`, `CODE-FIXED`, `DETECTION-DELTA`, `POLICY-DELTA`, `SCOPE-DELTA`,
210	`WAIVER-DELTA`, `EVIDENCE-DELTA`, `INDETERMINATE`; each entry also records
211	`presence` at every pivot and `subsequentDeltas` (later axes at which it changed
212	again). Deleting a waiver while adding a bug therefore yields one `WAIVER-DELTA` and
213	one `CODE-NET-NEW`; a bug introduced and simultaneously hidden by disabling the rule
214	is `CODE-NET-NEW` with `subsequentDeltas=[policy]`.
215	
216	**Detector union.** Comparison covers the union of baseline and current detectors.
217	Added detectors set E0 false. Removed detectors require the actual current-trusted
218	prior detector pivot and set E1–E4 false; E0 must never be substituted with B.
219	Consequently a new bug hidden by removing its detector remains CODE-NET-NEW and
220	can gate. Missing prior execution is indeterminate, including detector removal.
221	
222	**Evidence axis.** Compare the exact bound `import2` identity sets per kind, with
223	payload/correspondence/scope/observation digests retained in each BoundImport.
224	Replacing an artifact with another of the same kind is still an evidence change
225	(`evidence-content-changed`). For a rule with declared `evidenceUse`: if required evidence is
226	absent on the current side the entry is `INDETERMINATE`
227	(`required-evidence-unavailable`) and the rule's coverage is unsatisfied; if
228	availability changed and the rule gates on either side, attribution is
229	`INDETERMINATE` (`evidence-availability-changed`); only for a non-gating rule may a
230	presence change be `EVIDENCE-DELTA`. Required evidence loss can never disappear as a
231	non-gating delta.
232	
233	**Audit profiles select gate semantics explicitly** (schema `AuditProfile`):
234	
235	| Profile | Gates CODE-NET-NEW | Gates newly live via policy/scope/waiver | Gates all current live | New waiver suppresses net-new | Rule gating under |
236	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
237	| `code-regression` (default for `audit`) | yes | no | no | no | baseline or current |
238	| `policy-change` | yes | yes | no | no | baseline or current |
239	| `full-current` | yes | yes | yes | yes | current only |
240	| `report-only` | no | no | no | yes | current only |
241	
242	A `CODE-NET-NEW` entry that is not live in current (hidden by a later policy/scope
243	change or by a waiver added in the same change) still gates under
244	`baseline-or-current` with `gateReason=code-net-new-policy-hidden`. Verdict is `fail`
245	if any entry gates, else `indeterminate` if any `INDETERMINATE` entry belongs to a
246	gating rule or a current gating rule has unsatisfied/unknown required Coverage or
247	evidence, else `pass`. Rule deficiencies are enumerated independently of findings;
248	zero emitted findings never establish complete analysis. Whole-comparison indeterminacy (unmapped project,
249	unsupported schema/recipe major, context document mismatch) performs no comparison
250	and emits zero entries with a typed remedy. Enum precedence never decides a gate.

254	## 4. Imported evidence: one wrapper, typed payloads (AR-11)
255	
256	There is exactly one import identity: `importId = 'import2:' + H('import', wrapper)`
257	where the wrapper is the foundation `import` descriptor (schemaVersion 2, kinds
258	`runtime|test|history|dependency|prepared`). Each kind admits exactly one canonical
259	payload domain. Native runtime/test/history formats are adapter inputs normalized
260	into the workflow-owned payload before wrapping.
261	
262	| Kind | Admitted payload domain | Owner |
263	|---|---|---|
264	| runtime | `workflow.import-payload.runtime.v1` | workflow |
265	| test | `workflow.import-payload.test.v1` | workflow |
266	| history | `workflow.import-payload.history.v1` | workflow |
267	| dependency | `native.import-payload.dependency-source.v1` | native |
268	| prepared | `native.import-payload.prepared-output.v1` | native |
269	
270	The closed registry names the exact schema document and JSON selector. Its
271	`payloadSchemaDigest` is raw SHA-256 of the entire schema document's bytes;
272	`payloadDigest` is raw SHA-256 of the canonical validated payload. The host validates
273	the selected payload, source correspondence, foundation scope descriptor,
274	BuildIdentityV1, ImportObservationV1 and wrapper using the trusted local schema
275	closure. Merely carrying a recognized payloadDomain is insufficient. Caller-supplied
276	schema bytes must equal the registry document exactly. No network schema resolution
277	is allowed. All auxiliary digests are raw SHA-256 of their canonical closed records;
278	those preimages are retained. The `import2` wrapper alone uses the H-domain recipe.
279	The same payload with different provenance or observation semantics is a different import.
280	
281	Any other pairing is `IMPORT.KIND_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH`; an unregistered payload schema is
282	`IMPORT.PAYLOAD_SCHEMA_UNREGISTERED`; no artifact-supplied schema is ever admitted.
283	`opensip import KIND PATH` is a mutation step with an import receipt; the user-named
284	PATH is a `UserInputPath` opened through the security unit's nofollow custody and
285	never enters identity; every path inside a payload is a strict `LogicalPath`.
286	
287	Source correspondence is mandatory (`IMPORT.MAPPING_REQUIRED`, `CONFIG.INVALID`):
288	the shared closed SourceCorrespondence union in common.schema.json,
289	`exact-snapshot` or `vcs-revision` with VCS/build/mapping fields. Staleness
290	against a Plan is a closed table (`StalenessRule`): snapshot-equal → `current`,
291	consumable; snapshot-differs / commit-differs → `stale`, unmapped-only;
292	commit-equal-dirty → `unverifiable`, unmapped-only; build-identity-differs →
293	`wrong-build`, unmapped-only. An equal clean commit is consumable only with an
294	admitted SourceMappingV1 whose source paths and hashes join the current snapshot
295	inventory; an equal commit without that mapping remains unmapped-only. Corrupt bytes → refused (`IMPORT.ARTIFACT_CORRUPT`).
296	Explicitly selecting a stale import for a Plan is `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`
297	with `IMPORT.STALE_FOR_PLAN` (2). Unmapped-only evidence may be listed and queried
298	but never feeds a predicate.
299	
300	**No-hits is not non-use.** Runtime subjects carry `observed-hit`,
301	`observable-unhit`, `unobservable` or `unmapped`. `observed-hit` supplies positive
302	execution evidence and `observable-unhit` supplies bounded negative evidence,
303	always together with the observation window and population; `unobservable`/`unmapped` never become unhit signals and the schema
304	refuses a hit count on them. One window never establishes universal non-use;
305	runtime coverage is never OpenSIP Coverage. History payloads are advisory priority
306	inputs unless a policy predicate explicitly declares `evidenceUse` for them.

310	## 5. Declarative policy DSL, authoring test, candidate → inspect → review
311	
312	**DSL.** `PolicyDocumentV1` is closed data: rules with a `ruleProgramRef`
313	(contribution, stable id, semantics major, program digest), `enabled`, `severity`
314	(`note|warning|error`), `gate`, a `subjectEnumeration` (universe, subject kind,
315	include/exclude globs over `LogicalPath` with only `*`, `?` and whole-segment `**`),
316	an `emitWhen` predicate tree and `evidenceUse` declarations. Predicates are exactly
317	the evaluator's set: atoms `exists|none|count-at-most|all-covered` over a relation,
318	minimum resolution and typed field filters (`eq|neq|in|prefix|glob|gte|lte`), plus
319	`and|or|not`, depth ≤ 8, ≤ 64 nodes per rule, ≤ 512 rules. Evaluation is strong
320	Kleene: under incomplete Coverage `exists` is true on a match else indeterminate,
321	`none` false on a match else indeterminate, `count-at-most` false above N else
322	indeterminate, `all-covered` indeterminate. A true predicate emits a finding; false
323	is a retained no-match; an indeterminate gating rule is a typed deficiency. An atom
324	over imported evidence must be declared in `evidenceUse`; required evidence absent
325	makes the rule indeterminate, optional evidence absent is disclosed as
326	`IMPORT.ABSENT_FOR_PREDICATE` and is not a gating deficiency. There is no string
327	expression, hook, script, include or exec key; any such key is a schema violation
328	(`POLICY.IMPERATIVE_KEY_REFUSED`). Policy, ScopeDocumentV1 and resolved WaiverSetV1
329	digests are raw SHA-256 of their canonical closed documents, retained as blobs.
330	The compiled RuleProgramV1 separately hashes its policy digest and ordered rule
331	programs to proof.ruleProgramDigest; these are auxiliary hashes, not H identities.
332	
333	**Waivers.** A waiver targets a fingerprint or `(ruleId, subjectPath)` with a reason
334	and `expires` (date or null). Expiry and duplicates are resolved at **Plan
335	construction** against the admitted trust clock: expired waivers leave the effective
336	set and are disclosed (`POLICY.WAIVER_EXPIRED`), two waivers on one target refuse
337	(`POLICY.DUPLICATE_WAIVER`, `CONFIG.INVALID`), and the Plan's `waiverDigest` is that of
338	the *resolved* effective set, keeping evaluation pure. `opensip waive` is the explicit
339	tracked-intent write; nothing writes a waiver implicitly.
340	
341	**Authoring test.** `opensip policy test SUITE` is Query class. A suite supplies the
342	candidate policy, waivers, an `asOfDate`, optional test-only overrides and cases with
343	typed fact fixtures (subjects, facts, declared Coverage, available evidence kinds) or
344	a bounded source fixture. Facts cases are evaluated by the deterministic fixture
345	verifier (the finite declarative fixture evaluator; this is reference evidence, not
346	qualification of the production evaluator or native providers); sources cases run only under an ephemeral non-authoritative Plan with
347	bundled providers and otherwise report `not-executable`. Expectations are
348	`finding{ruleId,minCount,maxCount,subjects}`, `no-finding`, `verdict`, `indeterminate`.
349	The result (`policytest2:`) records candidate and effective digests, resolver
350	acceptance and refusals, applied overrides, waiver resolution and
351	`enforcementUnchanged=true`; the same suite always yields the same result identity.
352	
353	**Candidate → inspect → review (Map side).** `opensip candidates` lists
354	`Candidate` records derived from one sealed Run: findings plus advisory kinds
355	(`clone-candidate`, `low-confidence-unused`, `runtime-unhit`, `history-stale`) with an
356	evidence level. Only a finding on a gating rule is `controlBearing`. `opensip inspect`
357	returns a bounded `InspectionBundle` (≤ 4096 facts, Coverage, imports, limitations).
358	`opensip review join` records a `ReviewDisposition` (`accept|reject|defer`, reviewer
359	principal human/model/policy-rule, note, `suppressUntil` ≤ 365 days) as a mutation
360	with a receipt. The disposition schema admits no verdict, Run, baseline or
361	authorization field: review can never mint a Control verdict or authorize a repair.
362	`reject`/`defer` suppress the candidate from listings until `suppressUntil` or until
363	its fingerprint changes; expired suppressions resurface with `previouslyReviewed`.
364	`opensip review brief` is an advisory, bounded (≤ 1000) ordering labelled with its
365	producer (a model producer names its `closure2`); truncation is explicit.

369	## 6. Repair preview, apply, verify (AR-08)
370	
371	Three separately authorized steps; schemas in `repair.schema.json`.
372	
373	**Preview** (`repair-preview`, Query class) requires an **authoritative** evidence Run
374	(`REPAIR.EVIDENCE_RUN_NOT_AUTHORITATIVE` for ephemeral) whose availability is retained
375	and whose sealed assurance is replayable (else the plan is not applicable with
376	`REPAIR.EVIDENCE_RUN_UNAVAILABLE`), a recipe closure admitted under current trust
377	(`REPAIR.RECIPE_TRUST_REVOKED`; an absent admission is also refused), targets present in that Run, and a live tree equal to
378	the Run's snapshot (`REPAIR.SOURCE_MOVED`). It emits `RepairPlanV1`
379	(`repairplan2:` = `H('workflow.repair-plan', descriptor)`) bound to `snapshot2`,
380	`run2`, `plan2`, exact per-file edits (`replace|delete|create`, preimage digest from

380	`run2`, `plan2`, exact per-file edits (`replace|delete|create`, preimage digest from
381	the snapshot inventory, postimage digest and bytes; ≤ 4096 files, ≤ 16 MiB each,
382	≤ 64 MiB total), evidence requirements, the recipe's permitted edit scope (an edit
383	outside it is `REPAIR.EDIT_OUTSIDE_PERMITTED_SCOPE`), `applicable`, unmet
384	preconditions and limitations. Destructive unused-code recipes additionally require
385	native closed-world resolution evidence; an advisory similarity or runtime-cold
386	signal alone never authorizes deletion. Preview never writes.
387	
388	**Apply** (`repair-apply`, mutation) is bound to the exact `repairPlanId`, base
389	snapshot and project by a security-unit authorization (`REPAIR.CONSENT_NOT_BOUND`);
390	CI requires policy consent. Current recipe trust and live authorization are checked
391	again immediately before apply. It journals `RepairApplyJournalV1` through
392	`PREPARING → STAGED → APPLYING → APPLIED → COMMITTED`: every postimage is written to a
393	same-directory temp and digest-verified, every preimage is re-verified against the
394	live file (`REPAIR.TARGET_PREIMAGE_MISMATCH` leaves `FAILED_CLEAN`), renames proceed in
395	ascending path order, then the tree is re-snapshotted (`appliedSnapshotId`) and the
396	receipt written. A fault during `APPLYING` restores every renamed target
397	(`FAILED_ROLLED_BACK`, rollback `completed`); a renamed target that is neither
398	preimage nor postimage is `RECOVERY_BLOCKED` with the paths listed and no automatic
399	action. Replaying apply with the same idempotency key returns the completed receipt
400	with a new replay delivery receipt and `replayed=true`; the original is preserved.
401	
402	**Recover** (`repair-recover`) is a closed table over journal state: PREPARING/STAGED
403	→ discard temps (`FAILED_CLEAN`); APPLYING → roll back renamed (`FAILED_ROLLED_BACK`)
404	or block if a target is unrecognized; APPLIED/INDETERMINATE → verify every exact
405	postimage and the complete applied-path set before re-snapshot and commit;
406	COMMITTED/FAILED_* → none; RECOVERY_BLOCKED → refuse (`HOST.IO_FAILURE`,
407	`REPAIR.RECOVERY_BLOCKED`, exit 4). Every recovery mutation requires an authorization
408	bound to this repairPlanId and journal requestId; inspection alone is read-only.
409	Restore verifies all available retained preimage hashes before its first write.
410	Corrupt bytes yield LEDGER.CORRUPT / REPAIR.PREIMAGE_CORRUPT (4) with no target change.
411	Unavailable bytes return an exact restore intent and REPAIR.RECOVERY_REQUIRES_BROKER,
412	without claiming rollback completed. Recovery never re-applies an edit.
413	
414	**Verify** (`verify`) always admits a **fresh snapshot** after apply; it never reuses
415	the pre-apply Run. If the fresh snapshot differs from `appliedSnapshotId` the step is
416	`REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` / `REPAIR.SOURCE_MOVED` and no Run is sealed; otherwise
417	it seals a new authoritative Run and reports `VerificationOutcome`
418	(applied/verified snapshot, targets remaining, net-new findings). A separate immutable VerificationLinkV1 binds receiptId, verificationRunId, both
419	snapshots and the verification request/step. The apply receipt is never rewritten
420	and remains retained if verification fails.

424	## 7. Explicitly authorized test execution (AR-08)
425	
426	Repository code execution is disabled by default. `opensip test run` (request class
427	`execution`) is admitted only when: the security unit admits a `RepoExecutionGrantV2`
428	with principal `P-TRUSTED-REPO`, execution class `test-runner`, bound to this
429	project, snapshot digest and the exact `argv` digest, expiry operation-end, never
430	inherited (`TEST.PRINCIPAL_NOT_ADMITTED` otherwise); CI uses a pre-existing policy
431	record (`TEST.INTERACTIVE_CONSENT_IN_CI`); `argv[0]` is a `LogicalPath` member of the
432	sealed snapshot or a member of the declared toolchain `closure2`
433	(`TEST.ARGV_NOT_IN_CLOSURE`); the working directory is the project root or a
434	`LogicalPath` inside it; the environment is constructed from an allowlist only, `PATH`
435	is never copied (`TEST.ENV_NOT_ALLOWLISTED`) and is set to the toolchain closure; and
436	the live tree still equals the `afterStep` snapshot. There is no shell string and no
437	interpolation anywhere in the schema.

441	table measures a primitive; a claimed enforcement without a measured primitive is
442	refused (`TEST.CONFINEMENT_CLAIM_REFUSED`). The mandatory sentence before spawn is

445	is recorded. The outcome is a `TestPayloadV1` wrapped as an `import2` of kind `test`
446	— evidence, never Coverage and never a verdict; a verdict may depend on it only
447	through a declared policy predicate. Imported independently prepared test results
448	are the supported alternative.

17	## S1. Authority, applicability and superseded selectors

20	chain acceptance, revocation, platform admission, migration and leases. Content
21	identity never proves custody. A signed document proves only that its signer
22	signed those bytes; whether the document is admitted is decided by the rules

56	## S3. Discovery and custody (AR-03)
57	
58	Discovery is deterministic over lstat/ACL results obtained through O_NOFOLLOW
59	handles: no environment variable, no `PATH`, no `HOME` (the account home comes
60	from the account database). Output is the closed `DiscoveryProvenanceV1`.
61	
62	The disposable discovery instrument accepts only its named host-observation keys:
63	required `invokingUid`, `accountHome`, `cwd`, `fs`; optional `ci`,
64	`trustProjectOwner`, `authorizedGroupIds`, `explicitProject`, `explicitResolved`,
65	`explicitJoins`, `configWorkspaceRoots`. Unknown/missing keys or wrong outer
66	scalar/container types are `DISCOVERY_OBSERVATION_SHAPE` instrument errors,
67	not public D9 input refusals. Boolean observations are exact booleans and uid/gid
68	observations are nonnegative integers, never coerced strings or booleans. The
69	lstat/ACL map remains a synthetic trusted observation, not proof of native custody.
70	Public invocation/configuration admission still precedes this host-only seam.
71	
72	**Custody of a directory** passes only if: it is a real directory (no symlink);
73	owner is the invoking uid or root; mode has no other-write bit; mode has no
74	group-write bit unless the directory's gid is in the explicitly authorized set;
75	no ACL write grant (POSIX ACL on Linux, `acl_get_fd_np` on macOS) to any
76	principal other than the invoker, root, or an authorized group; and the ACL was
77	readable. Mode bits alone never establish exclusion. **Custody of a config
78	file** adds: regular file, link count 1, at most 4 MiB. Group authorization
79	exists only through an explicit `--trust-group <gid>` invocation argument and
80	is recorded in provenance; configuration cannot grant it. `--trust-project-owner`
81	waives only the owner check and only with an explicit `--project` path.
82	
83	**Walk rule.** With `--project`, the resolved path is examined exactly once
84	(symlink resolution recorded). Otherwise, from the launch directory upward, at
85	most 256 levels: a custody failure at the launch directory refuses
86	(`PROJECT.ROOT_CUSTODY_REFUSED`); a custody failure at an ancestor is a
87	boundary and that ancestor is never examined for a config. At each passing
88	directory the config, if present, is custody-checked (failure refuses
89	`CONFIG.CUSTODY_REFUSED`; it is never skipped) and selects that directory
90	(`mode: config`). Boundaries after a directory without config, in precedence:
91	VCS marker (`.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `.jj`), account home, filesystem root, mount
92	change. A VCS boundary selects **that repository root** (`mode: vcs-default`),
93	never the launch directory, so default scope does not change with launch
94	directory. Home, root, mount and custody boundaries without any candidate
95	select the launch directory (`mode: cwd-default`).
96	
97	**Nested config is a deliberate project boundary (decided; ADV-3).** A config
98	file found below a VCS root is an author-declared project root and wins for
99	launches inside it; the walk never continues above a config. The enclosing
100	VCS-root project treats that directory exactly like a nested repository: it is
101	recorded in `nestedProjects`, automatic discovery never enters it (excluded
102	unit reason `INSIDE_NESTED_PROJECT`), and an explicit join crossing into it
103	refuses `PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID` (`JOIN_CROSSES_NESTED_PROJECT`). Scope
104	therefore depends only on which project a launch is inside, never on which
105	directory of one project. The alternative (VCS root always wins) was rejected
106	because it would silently ignore a config the repository author placed. Cases
107	`nested-config-inside-a-vcs-root-*` and
108	`explicit-join-crossing-into-a-nested-project-refuses`.
109	
110	**VCS data.** A `.git` indirection file (`gitdir:`) is data: its target is
111	recorded and never followed by discovery; VCS digests for the snapshot are the
112	identity unit's concern and read only inside custody.
113	
114	**Authority roots versus workspace units.** Two different things are
115	distinguished. A *project authority/custody root* is the selected root: one
116	custody domain, one ProjectId, one lease namespace. Repositories nested under
117	it are other custody roots: they are recorded as `nestedRepositories`, never
118	entered, and reachable only by their own `--project`; a join that crosses into
119	one refuses `PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID` (`JOIN_CROSSES_NESTED_REPOSITORY`).
120	A *language workspace unit* is a directory inside the admitted root that
121	carries a manifest marker: `Cargo.toml`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` or
122	`jsconfig.json` (markers may co-locate; a unit lists all its markers). Units are
123	discovered **automatically** for the zero-config full product, with precedence:
124	
125	| Source | Provenance `unitSource` | Custody failure |
126	|---|---|---|
127	| repeatable CLI `--workspace-root PATH` overrides | `explicit-joins` | refuses (explicit intent) |
128	| admitted Config2 `discovery.workspaceRoots` (foundation product-configuration schema v2) | `config-workspace-roots` | refuses |
129	| marker scan of the admitted root | `automatic` | unit excluded, recorded in `excludedUnits` with the reason |
